447: Built around Huron Blackheart, Chosen, Defilers, Abaddon, Vashtorr, Masters of the Maelstrom, and waves of Cultist Mobs, this list runs Cabal of Chaos with Fellhammer Siege-Host as a secondary detachment, combining psyker-boosted shooting with army-wide ranged damage mitigation. The plan is to flood the midboard with expendable Cultists and Red Corsairs screening while Defilers and Dark Pact-empowered psykers pour firepower into priority targets, with Huron and Chosen hunting isolated units and Abaddon closing out combats. Fellhammer's wound-roll subtraction makes the horde remarkably durable against mid-strength guns — the kind of anti-infantry spam that typically shreds mass bodies gets blunted wholesale, letting the screen survive long enough to score. Elite elite-delete lists that ignore horde durability and target the key characters with high-Toughness-clearing weapons can strip out the damage engines before the Dark Pact engine gets rolling.
448: Built around Venomcrawlers, Defilers, Forgefiends, Vashtorr the Arkifane, and Warpsmiths, this list runs both Cabal of Chaos and Soulforged Warpack to stack Dark Pact buffs across a wall of Daemon Vehicles, with Cultist Mobs and Chaos Bikers providing cheap board presence and mobility. The engine is Soulforged Warpack's Dark Pact contract: each vehicle that invokes it gains +1 to wound on ranged attacks and +2 Attacks in melee, turning already-threatening chassis into overloaded kill platforms that punish any army that lets them reach fighting range intact. It excels against mechanised and elite lists — the combination of mobile anti-armour volume from multiple Venomcrawlers and Defilers creates an anti-tank overload that few armoured forces can weather. Its vulnerability is aggressive alpha-strike pressure and screen-denial: if opponents strip the Cultist and Biker screens early, the Daemon Vehicles are exposed to focus fire before their Dark Pacts can fire off.
450: Built around Lady Malys, Lelith Hesperax, Drazhar, and wall-to-wall Wyches and Incubi packed into Venoms and Raiders, this is a Wych Cult skimmer-rush list running Exhibition Of Slaughter and Skysplinter Assault together. The engine is disembark-and-delete: units pile out of transports to gain Lance on melee and Ignores Cover on shooting, while Exhibition Of Slaughter grants Lethal Hits on all Wych Cult melee attacks against non-Monsters and non-Vehicles, letting cheap Wyches punch well above their points and Incubi shred elite infantry outright. It punishes armies that rely on cover saves or spread-thin screening, since the disembark trigger strips cover and the sheer volume of Lethal Hits attacks overwhelms units that depend on armour to survive melee. A hard alpha strike or anything that dismounts the infantry before they disembark collapses the combo — crack the transports early and the kill chain never ignites.
466: Built around winged Daemon Princes of Slaanesh, Fulgrim, Lucius the Eternal, and Lord Exultants driving Infractors, Flawless Blades, and Noise Marines forward in Rhinos, this is a Coterie of the Conceited list that bets Pact points on its own kill output each round. The engine is the pledge mechanic: accurately forecasting enemy unit destruction generates Pact points that fuel the army's snowballing power, so the list commits to aggressive, precise killing rather than passive objective trading, using mobile melee and ranged threats to hit multiple units simultaneously. It punishes mid-table brawl lists that present numerous small or medium units — exactly the kind of target spread that makes pledges easy to hit while Defilers and anti-armour tools handle heavier pieces. It cracks open against armies that can hide units, deny kills through resilience or screen stacking, and force underperformed pledges, collapsing the Pact point engine before it gains momentum.
473: Built around multiple Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminators, Strike Squads, Grand Master Voldus, a Grand Master, Brotherhood Chaplain, and Interceptor Squads, this list runs the Argent Assault detachment to give Paladin Squads +1 to wound against high-toughness targets when their Strength would otherwise fall short. The plan is to flood the midboard with mobile elite infantry across multiple threat vectors — Interceptors repositioning to pressure objectives while Paladins and Terminators drive into fights where the wound-roll bonus makes them punch above their weight. It punishes lists built around durable, high-toughness targets like monsters and vehicles by converting what should be awkward wound rolls into consistent damage, especially when the Brotherhood Chaplain layers further fight-phase support. However, elite melee armies that can dictate fight priority, strip Paladins before they swing, or screen out the charge angles will expose just how much this build depends on getting the right matchups to land.
481: Built around the Knight Castellan and Knight Destrier, this list leans hard into the Dominus Foebreakers detachment's core rule: Dominus units gain +1 to hit against targets sheltering in terrain, punishing the cover-hugging screens and objective campers that define most competitive deployments. The plan is to advance aggressively with fast Knights while the Castellan hammers entrenched units out of terrain features, converting terrain-abuse into raw kill efficiency that snowballs into primary score. It punishes castle-style gunlines and screen-dependent armies especially hard, since the hit bonus directly dismantles their defensive geometry. The list cracks when faced with open-board aggression or elite melee threats that ignore cover entirely, leaving the Dominus bonus irrelevant and the relatively low model count exposed to attrition.
480: Built around packs of Armiger Warglaives and Helverins supported by a Knight Castellan, this is a wall of stomping steel that bleeds anti-armour firepower from every angle at every range band. The plan is to flood the board with mobile chassis that punish any opponent who can't credibly threaten multiple heavy targets simultaneously — Warglaives knife forward in melee while Helverins and the Castellan layer sustained ranged damage, collectively overloading any single threat-removal budget. It punishes elite armoured lists badly, forcing opponents into anti-tank overload decisions where something always gets through. Swarms of cheap bodies or mass mortal-wound output crack it open, since the build has limited model count to contest objectives and no efficient way to clear hordes before they screen out scoring lanes.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortress, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a Kâhl, this list packs elite infantry and heavy vehicles into a dense mid-board castle operating under the Hearthguard Covenant, re-rolling wound rolls of 1 on ranged attacks within 9" for its core KÂHL and HEARTHGUARD units. The win condition is choking the midfield with durable bodies and layered firepower — Hernkyn Pioneers and Yaegirs screen forward while the castle grinds enemies apart at close range, converting kills into YP to fuel secondary detachment abilities. It punishes elite low-model armies that can't shift multiple overlapping tough units efficiently, drowning them in short-range firepower from Thunderkyn and Ironkin Steeljacks before they can thin the herd. Spread-out, objective-racing lists that avoid the 9" bubble — or alpha-strike armies that can delete the castle's anchor elements in one turn — expose the build's limited range and fragility when the tight formation is forced to sprawl.
482: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Knight Castellans, Armiger Helverins, Knight Crusaders, and Cerastus Knight Lancers under the Freeblade Company detachment, this is a highly mobile wall of Knights that passively heals through attrition — every model regains a wound each Command phase and carries Feel No Pain 6+, making the army substantially tougher than its wounds suggest. The win condition is layered firepower across multiple threat vectors simultaneously: Castellans and Crusaders deliver punishing long-range anti-armour while Lancers and Warglaives sprint into melee to threaten flanks and contest objectives, forcing opponents to split fire across too many targets to remove any one efficiently. It punishes slow, fragile elite lists that cannot generate enough anti-tank volume to kill Knights faster than they regenerate, and the mobile toolkit handles everything from light infantry screens to heavy armour. It struggles against high-volume, high-strength shooting armies that can concentrate enough damage in a single phase to delete models before healing matters.
456: Built around Canoptek Wraiths, Ophydian Destroyers, and a full court of C'tan shards — Void Dragon, Nightbringer, and Deceiver — all supported by Technomancers, Canoptek Reanimators, and Nekrosor Ammentar, this Awakened Dynasty list runs an oppressive mass of durable, character-led threats that hit on 2s across the board. The plan is to flood mid-table with unkillable bodies, use C'tan and Destroyers as independent kill threats, and grind opponents out of scoring positions while Reanimators keep the castle continuously regenerating. It punishes low-damage, low-volume lists that can't clear multiple resilient multi-wound units simultaneously — spreading lethal threat across six-plus independent pieces makes priority targeting impossible. However, high-AP, high-volume shooting that can isolate and delete individual C'tan or strip Wraith blobs before Reanimation triggers will dismantle the engine piece by piece.
486: Built around nearly five squads of Boyz supported by Painboyz, Warbosses, Bigbosses, Ghazghkull Thraka, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Weirdboyz, Stormboyz, Kommandos, and Gretchin screening, this is the Green Tide detachment in its purest form — a wall of green bodies with 5+ invulnerable saves on any Boyz unit holding ten or more models. The plan is to flood every midboard objective simultaneously, keep Boyz squads above the ten-model threshold to maintain that invuln, and let Painboyz recycle wounds while Ghazghkull and Warbosses pump out the combat output needed to grind opponents off points. It absolutely punishes armies that rely on low-volume, high-AP shooting, because massed attacks below the wound threshold get soaked by sheer numbers and the layered invulnerable saves. However, high-volume mortal-wound output or blast weapons that carve squads below ten models collapse the invuln tier, and anything that can alpha-strike multiple Boyz mobs simultaneously before they engage will crack the horde wide open.
487: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, Beastboss, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Kill Rigs, and Mozrog Skragbad, with Gretchin flooding the backfield, this is Da Big Hunt — a wall of squig-riding savages that designates a single enemy Monster, Vehicle, or Character as Prey each Command phase, unlocking charge re-rolls for every Beast Snagga unit within 12" of it. The win condition is crashing multiple units into the designated Prey simultaneously, using stacked charge re-rolls to guarantee contact and then burying priority targets under massed attacks while Kill Rigs anchor mid-board objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — expensive vehicles and Characters become the Prey target, funneling the entire kill chain into the opponent's most critical piece each turn. Spreading across a wide, cheap footprint to deny Prey selection and board control, or fielding fast chaff screens that prevent reliable charge windows, is what cracks this list open.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, two-plus Infernus Squads, a Land Raider Redeemer, and paired Librarians supported by Adrax Agatone, Bladeguard Veterans, Sternguard, and Scout screening, running Forgefather's Seekers with a Librarius Conclave secondary detachment. The plan is to push Infernus Squads forward on Seeker's Companions actions while the Redeemer delivers them into 12" threat range, where Forgefather's Seekers bumps all ranged Strength by 1 and adds Assault, letting the flamers and special weapons shred through infantry hordes and light vehicles at close range backed by the Divination or Pyromancy disciplines from the Librarians. It absolutely punishes dense infantry armies and mid-toughness multi-wound targets that can't avoid clustering inside 12". High-armour lists or elite armies that can force engagements at range beyond 12" and punish the slow Redeemer delivery mechanism will crack this open before the fire gets rolling.
488:
Built around Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Big Mek Dakkarigsm Flash Gitz, Lootas, and Tankbustas hauled forward in Trukks, with Gretchin and Meks flooding the board, this is a Dread Mob gunline that hits like a brawler.

The engine is the Dread Mob detachment's randomised weapon enhancement table — every time a Mek, Walker, or Grots Vehicle unit activates, it rolls for a combat buff or selects one deliberately, letting Big Meks and Dakkarigsm chain reliable lethal output while Tankbustas deliver mobile anti-armour pressure from Trukks and Lootas anchor a heavy firebase.

It punishes mid-table armies that want to trade shooting, drowning them in sheer volume with Gitfinder Gogglez sharpening accuracy, and the mass Gretchin screen makes it brutally hard to alpha-strike the expensive guns off the table.

Extended elite melee lists that can crack the screen and tie up the gunline in combat are the real threat, because once Lootas and Flash Gitz are stuck in the fight, the carefully managed weapon-table selection collapses into chaos.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar, Victrix Honour Guard, Repulsor Executioners, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, supported by a deep bench of Scout, Intercessor, Incursor, and Jump Pack Assault Intercessor infantry, this list runs the Blade of Ultramar detachment to cycle Combat Doctrines across the game. The engine is Calgar's ability to re-select Doctrines, letting the list shift between shooting and assault buffs as needed while Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts hammer armour from range and Jump Pack Assault Intercessors pressure objectives mid-board. It punishes gunline and mechanised lists that present clustered armour targets, overwhelming them with layered anti-tank from multiple angles while cheap infantry screens deny easy counter-charges. It cracks under elite melee alpha strikes that can isolate and delete the Honour Guard bubble before Calgar's Doctrine cycling pays off.
478: Built around Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Logan Grimnar, Wolf Guard Terminators, Thunderwolf Cavalry, Arjac Rockfist, Wulfen with Storm Shields, Intercessors, and Gladiator Lancers, this is a transported melee-heavy brawler running primarily Saga of the Great Wolf. The plan is to flood the mid-table with durable, hard-hitting infantry delivered by transports, using Thunderwolves and Wulfen as shock cavalry to hit flanks while Bjorn and Lancers provide layered anti-armour support, with Grimnar buffing the kill chain across multiple fronts. It punishes slow, static gunlines that cannot screen the mid-table, overwhelming them with simultaneous threats from multiple high-toughness, high-damage units before they can prioritise correctly. It cracks open against fast, high-volume mortal-wound output or elite alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete the transport bubble early, leaving the infantry stranded without their delivery mechanism.
428: Built around the Twin Lance, multiple Riptides, Broadsides, Crisis Starscythes, Ghostkeels, and Stealth Battlesuits, screened and spotted by Pathfinders and Piranhas, this is a Mont'Ka gunline that moves aggressively forward. Mont'Ka grants [ASSAULT] across the army for the first three battle rounds, letting every unit advance and still fire at full effect, while Guided units from the For the Greater Good network gain [LETHAL HITS], turning already-heavy firepower into a lethal kill chain against armoured targets. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — the combination of mobile anti-tank volume and Lethal Hits shreds tough multi-wound units before they can close. Against cheap, fast screens and horde armies that can absorb shooting and contest objectives early, the list struggles to clear bodies efficiently enough to deny scoring.
483: Built around Neurolictors, Lictors, Broodlords, Genestealers, Von Ryan's Leapers, Deathleaper, Zoanthropes, Hyperadapted Raveners, Raveners, and Hormagaunts, supported by Biovores and a Neurotyrant, this is a deep-striking swarm that uses the Ambush Predators detachment to flood the board from multiple angles simultaneously. The win condition is coordinated mid-table pressure — Lictors and Neurolictors drop in to crack characters and expose backfield units while Genestealers and Broodlords surge forward to dominate objectives through sheer combat volume. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't screen every vector, as the deep-strike threat forces impossible pre-deployment decisions and leaves exposed flanks for Raveners and Leapers to exploit. It cracks open against castle gunlines with layered screening, which can spot and shoot arriving deep strikers before the melee engine engages, or against armies that trade efficiently into its numerous but individually fragile units.
490: Built around Sekhetar Robots, Defilers, Forgefiends, Tzaangor Shamans, and Exalted Sorcerers on Disc, this Sekhetar Cohort list pairs its robot battleline with Warpforged Cabal vehicles into a psychic-buffed fire platform. Psykers orbit within 12" to grant the robots +1 WS through Infusion while simultaneously unlocking Warpforged Cabal's full triple-reroll suite on Defilers and Forgefiends, turning every activation into a high-efficiency damage roll. The build punishes slow armoured gunlines by overloading their anti-tank budget across multiple [PSYCHIC]-keyword vehicle threats that fight and shoot with consistent rerolls. It cracks open when fast harassment strips the psyker bubbles early, collapsing both the WS bonus and the premium reroll tier simultaneously.
489: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Rubric Marines holding ground, Sekhetar Robots as a Psychic-attack battleline, Tzaangors screening, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows skimming at range, and a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings as a mobile hammer, this list runs the Hexwarp Thrallband detachment to extend Flow of Magic across No Man's Land the moment it contests midfield objectives. The plan is to lock in that zone-of-control early, fuelling Ritual chains and Psychic synergies while layered shooting from Fatecaster bows and Sekhetar Robots' Psychic-tagged attacks bleeds opponents dry before they can trade efficiently. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — the combination of Empyric Onslaught, high-AP Psychic attacks, and a durable horde screen means expensive units melt faster than they can return damage. Mass mortal-wound immunity, volume anti-horde shooting, and aggressive deep-strike pressure can overwhelm the flow of magic control, leaving the entire Psychic engine starved of its fuel before the army's shooting can compensate.
427: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Ghostkeels, and a full suite of Crisis variants alongside Riptides and Commander Farsight, this list runs the Advanced Acquisition Cadre detachment to let its hidden units — Pathfinders and Stealth Battlesuits — shoot without breaking concealment, then layers in Retaliation Cadre on three-quarters of lists to sharpen Battlesuit firepower at close range, boosting Strength within 12" and AP within 9". The win condition is mobile anti-armour overload: Coldstar Commanders and The Twin Lance reposition aggressively while Crisis Sunforges, Fireknives, and Starscythes delete hard targets at close quarters, with Riptides anchoring mid-table scoring. It punishes mechanised and elite lists brutally, stacking AP bonuses into already strong Battlesuit weapons against anything wearing heavy armour. Horde armies that flood screens force the Battlesuits into suboptimal ranges, and anything that collapses the hidden bubble on Pathfinders early strips the target-marking network the kill chain depends on.
484: Built around Norn Assimilators, Norn Emissaries, Pyrovores, Psychophages, Biovores, Ripper Swarms, and Tyranid Primes with lash whip, this is a regenerating attrition engine running the Assimilation Swarm detachment, where HARVESTER units continuously restore wounds and return destroyed models to keep the horde perpetually topped up. The win condition is outlasting opponents through sustained board presence — flooding mid-table with durable, self-replenishing bodies while Biovore chip damage and Norn monster threats force impossible priority decisions. It punishes lists that rely on burst damage or single-phase alpha strikes, since the regeneration loop undoes concentrated firepower and makes trading unfavorable for most conventional gunlines. It cracks under sustained, distributed high-volume shooting across multiple turns, or against armies that can deny HARVESTER auras through positioning and deny the regeneration cycle before the swarm reaches critical mass.
500: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Neophyte Hybrids, Acolyte Hybrids (both hand flamer and autopistol variants), Atalan Jackals, Hybrid Metamorphs, Achilles Ridgerunners, Benefictus, Reductus Saboteurs, and the Patriarch, this is a sprawling horde gunline that floods the board with cheap bodies while Ridgerunners provide consistent long-range anti-armour pressure. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Purestrains and Acolytes threaten punishing charges while Ridgerunners and Saboteurs dismantle vehicles, forcing opponents to split resources across too many vectors simultaneously. Neophytes sheltering inside terrain regenerate wounds each Command phase under Xenocult Masses, making mid-board objective holds brutally difficult to clear efficiently. The list cracks open against elite alpha-strike armies that can surgically delete key threat units before the layered pressure fully assembles, as individual units carry modest staying power outside their terrain-anchored Neophyte core.
518: Built around Skorpekh Destroyers, Skorpekh Lords, Lokhust Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Technomancer, and Canoptek Wraiths, this is a wall-to-wall Destroyer Cult list running Cursed Legion to stack Strength bonuses across every unit, with most lists adding Skyshroud Spearhead to give Tomb Blades deep strike and post-ingress accuracy. The win condition is a cascading kill chain: Cursed Legion's triggered Strength boost rewards the first destroyed or half-strength unit each turn, so the list hunts easy targets first to supercharge subsequent attacks against harder ones. It punishes mid-density armies that cannot screen every angle simultaneously — the Ophydians threaten flanks while Lokhust units handle ranged priority targets, and the sheer volume of Destroyer Cult bodies makes anti-tank overload nearly impossible to achieve cleanly. Saturating armies and fast melee screens crack it open, since tying up Skorpekh units before the cascade triggers denies the engine entirely.
503: Built around Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, a Librarian in Terminator Armour, an Ancient in Terminator Armour, and Intercessor Squads, this is a slow-moving Terminator brick supported by psychic buffs and a sturdy infantry screen. The Librarian cycles through Psychic Disciplines each battle round — Divination for re-rolls on the way in, Biomancy to close distance faster, or Pyromancy to torch screens — while the Ancient keeps the brick resilient and punishes removal. It punishes gunline armies and transport-heavy lists that expect to trade efficiently at range, because the Terminators absorb punishment and eventually deliver an overwhelming melee threat that mass small-arms fire struggles to shift. However, the build cracks open against high-mobility, multi-vector threat lists that can isolate the Terminator blobs before they close, since the brick's slow advance leaves objectives vulnerable and a single disrupted approach lane can strand the entire engine.
517: Built around near-double Doomsday Arks, the Silent King, Technomancers keeping them alive, Canoptek Wraiths, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list is a mobile, objective-anchored firing platform that punishes anything that contests markers. The Starshatter Arsenal's detachment ability turns every objective zone into a kill zone — vehicles gain Assault to shoot after advancing while hitting more reliably on anything near an objective, letting Doomsday Arks pump out heavy firepower without standing still, supported by Chrono-impedance Fields slowing enemy counterpressure. Mechanically mobile anti-armour threats like Wraiths and Ophydian Destroyers pressure flanks while the guns deal with heavy vehicles and monsters that try to hold objectives at range. Lists that can alpha-strike the Arks before Technomancers reanimate them, or drown the screens in high-volume melee, crack this build open before the firepower engine gets rolling.
504: Built around Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, Intercessor Squads, and Scout Squads led by a Lieutenant with combi-weapon, this list floods the board with fast, hard-hitting skimmer firepower backed by a solid infantry core. The win condition is mobile anti-armour overload — Hammerstrikes hunt vehicles and monsters from turn one while Speeders reposition constantly to maintain optimal firing angles, with Scouts and Intercessors holding objectives to bank primary points. It punishes armour-heavy lists brutally, stacking skimmer fire into priority targets before they can respond, while the infantry screen denies easy early pressure. Against elite melee threats or fast alpha-strike armies that can close the distance before the guns speak, the relatively fragile skimmer chassis becomes a liability fast.
530: Built around Vertus Praetors, Shield-Captains on Dawneagle Jetbikes, Allarus Custodians, Shield-Captains in Allarus Terminator Armour, and Telemon Heavy Dreadnoughts, this is an elite mid-table brawler that leverages exceptional individual model quality across both fast jetbike and heavy terminator platforms. The plan is to dominate the mid-board through overlapping threat vectors — jetbikes pressure flanks and contest at speed while Allarus units deep-strike or slam into priority targets, generating kill points and holding primary through sheer staying power. It punishes attrition-focused lists that lack the damage density to efficiently remove elite T6+ multi-wound models, turning every trade into a numbers advantage. Mass high-AP shooting or melee that bypasses individual model durability cracks it open, as the low model count means losing even one or two key pieces collapses board coverage.
525: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, with Outriders, Scout Squads, and Incursors filling out the battleline, this is a Company of Hunters and Darkflight Pursuit list that floods the board with fast vehicles firing at full effect after Advancing or Falling Back. The engine is relentless pressure: Mounted units Advance-and-shoot while Ignores Cover strips defensive bonuses from entrenched infantry, letting the Vengeances and Thunderstrikes hammer anything that tries to hold cover and score. It punishes static gunlines and mechanized lists that lean on cover or Dense Terrain by removing those protections entirely while outpacing anything that tries to reposition away. Armies that can deliver high-volume, high-AP melee into the speeders early — particularly alpha-strike deep strikers — can crack the fragile vehicle chassis before Company of Hunters mobility becomes a decisive advantage.
527:
Built around Skorpekh Lords, Nekrosor Ammentar, Skorpekh Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, Lokhust Destroyers, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, and Ophydian Destroyers, this is an all-destroyer murder-machine that floods the board with fast, hard-hitting melee and ranged threat vectors simultaneously.

The win condition is layered kill pressure: Ophydian Destroyers deep strike into backfield threats while Skorpekh units crash into midfield, forcing opponents to split fire across multiple dangerous units rather than focusing any single piece down.

This punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot generate enough return fire to strip the board of Destroyer units before they tear through their targets across multiple phases.

Its weakness is mass volume shooting — cheap chaff that bricks up movement corridors denies the mobility this build depends on, and high-volume small-arms can chip away at mid-sized Destroyer squads faster than they can regenerate pressure.
529: Built around Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Blood Claws, Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Ragnar Blackmane, Wulfen with Storm Shields, Grey Hunters, and Wolf Scouts, this Saga of the Beastslayer list is a transport-heavy, character-dense brawler that floods the midboard with aggressive infantry. The engine is Lethal Hits on every attack against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles — meaning elite enemy pieces and heavy armour bleed out faster than expected the moment the pack closes in, with the Beastslayer tally extending that bonus army-wide once triggered. It punishes elite-model armies and character-heavy lists hard, where Lethal Hits on high-value targets compounds across multiple combat phases into severe attrition that expensive units can't absorb. It cracks when faced with volume-damage hordes or ranged alpha strikes that strip the transport shells before the wolves reach combat, leaving exposed infantry without the board position to score or brawl effectively.
521: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Ghostkeels, Pathfinders, Riptides, Broadsides, and a full Crisis suite — Sunforge, Starscythe, Fireknife — alongside Vespid Stingwings and Commander Farsight anchoring an elite alien-auxiliary core, this list floods the table with hard-to-shift battlesuit threats at every range band. The plan is to use Pathfinders to Spot targets for coordinated guided fire while mobile Coldstar Commanders and Crisis suits hunt armour across the midfield, generating kills that convert into scoring pressure. It punishes armour-heavy and elite-infantry lists through anti-tank overload — multiple Riptides and Broadsides force impossible target-priority decisions, and Vespid Stingwings screen out deep-strike threats. Horde armies that can drown the board in bodies and tie up suits in melee, bleeding actions and denying the standoff range this list craves, are its hardest counter.
441: Built around Azrael, multiple Librarians (including Terminator-armoured ones), Inner Circle Companions, Deathwing Knights, Sternguard Veterans, and Scout and Intercessor screens, all running Librarius Conclave to cycle Psychic Disciplines each round. The engine is a tight castle: Azrael bubbles the core brick while Librarians rotate between Divination's hit/wound re-rolls to push damage and Biomancy's movement buff to reposition the melee hammer when needed, with Temporal Corridor and Fusillade enhancements accelerating key units into scoring or kill positions. This list punishes slower, durable infantry blocks that expect to weather a turn before hitting back — the combination of re-roll support and Inner Circle Companions hitting in melee dismantles static gunlines before they can dictate range. It cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can fragment the castle early, since the build's synergies collapse when Azrael's bubble is disrupted and individual units are isolated.
550: Built around multiple Lords of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, Be'lakor, and Screamers as fast-moving objective harassers, with Flamers providing short-range threat, this list runs Lords Of The Warp alongside Scintillating Legion to stack re-rolls through Flux tokens on its Tzeentch units while boosting Character OC and Leadership across the board. The engine is mobile pressure: Screamers jet across the map to contest and flip objectives while Lords of Change and Kairos project layered mortal-wound and shooting threat, spending Flux tokens to fish for devastating rolls at critical moments. It punishes low-model-count elite armies by flooding objectives with high-OC Characters and fast screens that are individually dangerous to ignore. Blast-heavy or volume-fire lists that can strip Flux tokens faster than they're generated will expose the build's reliance on those re-rolls to survive difficult saves and output consistent damage.
551:
Built around Skarbrand, Rendmasters on Blood Throne, Bloodletters, Flesh Hounds, Bloodcrushers, and a Bloodthirster, this Blood Legion list plays an aggressive forward-pressure game with a wall of Khorne infantry and cavalry backed by Nurglings and Plaguebearers holding the backfield.

The win condition is the Blood Legion Surge mechanic: every time an opponent Advances or Normals within 6" of a Khorne unit, that unit lunges forward for free, collapsing the midboard and forcing unfavorable combats before the opponent is set up to receive them.

It punishes reactive, shooty armies that try to reposition — every Normal or Advance move becomes a trigger that drags the opponent into a meat grinder of layered lethal damage output from multiple elite combat threats simultaneously.

It cracks open against armies that can lock down the midboard at range without advancing, denying Surge triggers entirely and picking apart the horde piecemeal before the contact game begins.
445:
Built around Death Company Dreadnoughts, Death Company Marines with jump packs, Sanguinary Guard, Lemartes, a jump pack Captain, Intercessors, and Commander Dante, this is a high-mobility melee hammer that floods mid-board with airborne elite infantry backed by heavy walker support.

The plan is to charge multiple threats simultaneously — Lemartes buffing Death Company Marines into ferocious charge-turn combat while Dreadnoughts smash armour — converting that aggression into kill points and objective pressure in the same activation window.

It punishes slow, static armies that cannot screen their scoring units, overwhelming them with multiple simultaneous melee threats they cannot coherently answer before losing key objectives.

Where it cracks is against fast, shooting-heavy lists that can kite, strip Death Company before the charge, or screen out the Dreadnoughts — with no detachment consistently shaping its rules engine, its output can be inconsistent against well-prepared opponents.
459: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Leman Russ Vanquishers, Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, and Gaunt's Ghosts, this is a mobile armoured gunline running the Designation Force detachment, with roughly half of lists pairing it with either Hammer of the Emperor or Steel Hammer for a second detachment slot. The core engine is Signal Flares: Scout Sentinels and infantry smoke units push forward to designate targets, converting that scouting pressure into prioritised kill lanes for the massed Squadron armour sitting behind them, while Gaunt's Ghosts provide elite infantry leverage on objectives. It punishes ponderous armour-heavy lists that can't avoid presenting clean target priority — the layered long-range anti-tank from Vanquishers and Dorns simply dismantles them piece by piece. However, fast aggressive armies that can close into Engagement Range early disrupt the gunline's spacing and negate the clean firing lanes this build depends on to function.
465: Built around daemonettes, defilers, lords exultant, infractors, tormentors, flawless blades, and noise marines — all operating inside the Carnival of Excess detachment — this is a surging melee horde that keeps Emperor's Children and Legions of Excess units stacked within 6" of each other to maintain Empowered status, granting Sustained Hits across the board. The plan is to flood the midboard with Rhino-mounted infantry and daemonette screens, trigger Frenzied Host's +1 Strength on advancing battleline units, and grind opponents off objectives through sheer volume of Sustained Hits attacks. It punishes elite low-model-count armies by generating overwhelming attack output that anti-tank-heavy lists simply cannot trade into efficiently. Armies with strong shooting, area denial, or early alpha strike potential can disrupt the proximity bubble before it fully engages, leaving isolated units without Empowered and starved of the Sustained Hits that make the whole engine work.
534: Built around Sagitaurs scouting up 6" at game start, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hearthkyn Warriors packed into transports, this is a heavily armoured gunline that crashes forward into mid-table on turn one. The plan is to establish an early firing line using Scouts 6" on the Sagitaurs to claim midfield position, then layer Thunderkyn and transport-supported infantry firepower to grind opponents off objectives through sheer volume of durable, hard-hitting ranged output. It punishes slower, fragile armies that can't contest mid-table early, overwhelming them before they establish board presence. It struggles against fast alpha-strike lists or elite melee threats that can bypass the armoured shell and dismantle the infantry core before the gunline locks in.
546: Built around the Void Dragon, Nightbringer, Deceiver, and multiple Transcendent C'tan alongside Flayed Ones, Immortals, and Hexmark Destroyers, all operating under Hand of the Dynasty — which lets Immortals shoot after advancing and keeps them action-eligible — with roughly three-fifths of lists adding Hypercrypt Legion's end-of-turn repositioning and two-fifths running Pantheon of Woe's aura to strip enemy armour saves. The plan is to flood the board with unkillable Monster-tier threats that each demand dedicated answers, using the C'tan's natural durability and the detachment suite to teleport or reposition into scoring positions while the kill-pieces dismantle whatever the opponent over-commits to stopping them. It punishes mid-range gunlines and single-faction removal packages that simply cannot generate enough high-AP volume to down multiple C'tan in one turn, leaving objectives exposed. Armies with massed mortal-wound output or high-volume AP-2 or better attacks across multiple units can threaten several C'tan simultaneously, collapsing the durability shell before the scoring engine gets going.
544: Built around Skorpekh Lords leading Skorpekh Destroyers, supported by Nekrosor Ammentar, the Void Dragon, Illuminor Szeras, Lokhust Lords with Destroyer squads, the Silent King, and a durable screen of Wraiths and Warriors, this is an Awakened Dynasty list that gets +1 to Hit on every attack made by CHARACTER-led units. The win condition is overwhelming melee and shooting pressure across multiple threat vectors simultaneously — Skorpekh units crash into mid-board while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and the Void Dragon handle armour, making it nearly impossible for an opponent to prioritise correctly. The mobile toolbox profile punishes lists that commit to facing one threat type, since neutralising the melee wave exposes you to the anti-armour axis and vice versa. It struggles against lists that can isolate and delete individual units before they link up, as the synergy depends on delivering multiple pieces together rather than any single unstoppable unit.
526: Built around dual C'tan Shards (Void Dragon and Nightbringer), Lychguard, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Plasmancer, and an Overlord with Translocation Shroud, this list fields an elite, highly mobile toolkit of monsters and melee hammers across multiple detachments. The win condition is layered threat saturation — the C'tan demand immediate answers while Ophydian Destroyers tunnel into flanks and Lokhust Destroyers strip armor at range, forcing opponents into impossible priority decisions that bleed scoring opportunities. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count elite armies that lack the volume of removal needed to handle multiple durable, independent threats simultaneously. It cracks under dense, high-AP shooting that can focus down C'tan before their presence warps opponent positioning, or against screens deep enough to deny the close-range kill chain.
556: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, Beastboss, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Mozrog Skragbad, and waves of Boyz screaming forward in Trukks under the War Horde detachment, this is a wall-to-wall melee horde that turns every Ork melee weapon into a Sustained Hits 1 buzz-saw. The plan is to flood the midboard with bodies, use Snikrot and Trukk-delivered Boyz to contest early, then let the Beast Snagga core and monster characters grind through anything holding objectives. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot absorb the sheer volume of Sustained Hits 1 melee attacks across multiple combat phases. It cracks open against shooting-heavy lists that can strip Gretchin screens and isolate the characters before the green tide makes contact.
558: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek, massed Warbikers, Deffkoptas, Deffkilla Wartrikes, Boyz, and Stormboyz, this is a high-volume Speed Freeks brawler running primarily Kult Of Speed, which lets its cavalry and bike units shoot and charge freely after Advancing or Falling Back. The plan is to flood mid-table turn one with fast, hard-to-shift bodies, use Gretchin to hold home objectives cheaply, and grind opponents off primaries through sheer weight of attacks across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It punishes slow or static armies brutally — anything that can't redeploy or screen fast enough gets swarmed from multiple angles before it can concentrate firepower. Armies with strong volume anti-infantry that can delete whole squads efficiently, or elite deep-strike units that bypass the mob entirely, can crack the horde open by eliminating the scoring bodies before they establish mid-table dominance.
553: Built around Marneus Calgar, Victrix Honour Guard, Wardens of Ultramar, Scouts, Intercessors, and a core of Repulsor Executioners, this list blends an elite protective bubble with a heavy armoured gunline. The win condition is controlling objectives with durable, hard-to-shift infantry while Repulsor Executioners hammer armour and monsters from range, keeping pressure on the opponent's scoring zones throughout all battle rounds. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot contest multiple objectives simultaneously, as the combination of resilient bodyguard units and sustained tank fire creates an anti-tank overload few elite forces can absorb. It cracks open against aggressive screens and alpha-strike armies that can isolate Calgar's bubble early, stripping the protective synergy before the gunline can establish fire lanes.
533: Built around Crisis Sunforge and Starscythe Battlesuits, Coldstar Commanders, Stealth Battlesuits, the Twin Lance, Ghostkeels, Pathfinders, Vespid Stingwings, and Kroot Carnivores operating under the Experimental Prototype Cadre, which extends all Battlesuit Character ranged attacks by 6", letting Coldstars and similar pieces threaten from distances opponents can't easily punish. The plan is to leverage that extended reach alongside Kauyon's Sustained Hits 1 and Guided unit interactions in the mid-to-late game to delete priority targets from safety while Kroot and Vespid flood objectives and contest the midboard. This list punishes static, high-value target lists — elite infantry or heavy vehicle armies that can't easily close distance — because the range extension and Guided/Spotted chain let Tau delete expensive pieces before melee engagement is even possible. It cracks open under aggressive screen-clearing alpha strikes that collapse the Kroot and Vespid bubble early, exposing the Battlesuit core to close-range pressure where the range-extension advantage evaporates.
561: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Rubric Marines, Tzaangors, Sekhetar Robots, and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows operating under the Rubricae Phalanx detachment, which grants Rubricae models an extra point on their armour saves against any attack with a flat-1 Damage characteristic. The plan is to grind forward mid-board, soaking chip damage through that damage-1 immunity while layering shooting from multiple threat vectors — bows, robots, and Terminators — to extract value across a sustained game rather than winning a single decisive trade. This build punishes lists that rely on volume small-arms fire and mortal wounds to strip infantry, as those attacks simply bounce off the enhanced saves while the phalanx methodically clears objectives. High-flat-damage weapons that bypass the detachment's entire protection scheme — anything swinging at Damage 2 or higher — crack it open quickly, and the list's relatively slow, infantry-heavy footprint leaves it exposed to alpha strikes before it can establish board presence.
560: Built around Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sekhetar Robots, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and regular Sorcerers, this is a mass-horde psyker force that floods the board with bodies across multiple unit types. The plan is to drown opponents in layered threats — screening infantry control the mid-table while Sekhetar Robots and Enlightened apply persistent ranged pressure, letting Terminators and Rubrics grind through objectives behind a wall of expendable chaff. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear volume, as the sheer density of units and interlocking supporting characters make attrition deeply inefficient for the opponent. However, lists with high-volume mortal wound output or blast weapons that carve through clustered hordes can collapse the screen quickly and strand the slower Terminator core without cover.
573: Built around Sanguinary Priests buffing Sanguinary Guard, Assault Intercessors, Bladeguard Veterans, Death Company with jump packs, and Lemartes leading the charge, this is a mass-assault infantry list that uses the Liberator Assault Group's +2 Strength and +1 Attacks on charging units to turn every fight phase into a blender — Baal Predators and Intercessors hold ground and provide fire support while the jump-pack elements threaten every angle. The win condition is layered pressure: scouts and Intercessors screen objectives while multiple charging units simultaneously overwhelm key targets, converting the charge bonus into outsized damage across several combats per turn. It punishes slower gunlines and elite low-model-count armies that can't absorb the volume of boosted melee attacks hitting from multiple directions at once. It cracks open against fast armies that can deny or redirect charges turn after turn, stripping the detachment bonus and leaving the infantry exposed without their fight-phase spike.
571: Built around Skorpius Disintegrators, Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Skitarii Rangers, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Servitor Battleclades, and Onager Dunecrawlers, this is a layered heavy gunline that keeps its Tech-Priests alive through the Lords of the Forge detachment's 4+ invulnerable save and Feel No Pain 5+, while Cohort Cybernetica pushes Legio Cybernetica units forward with extra movement and boosted Objective Control. The win condition is sustained ranged attrition — Cawl and Thulia Ghuld stack buffs onto the Disintegrators and Ballistarii to grind opposing armies off objectives while Rangers and Battleclades hold ground cheaply. This build punishes mid-range shooty lists that lack the volume or AP to crack layered saves across multiple durable vehicle platforms simultaneously. It cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike armies that can close the distance fast and force the gunline to shoot at targets it was never positioned to engage efficiently.
577: Built around Warlock Skyrunners, Rangers, Warlock Conclaves, Shroud Runners, Eldrad Ulthran, War Walkers, and solo Warlocks, this list layers psychic support and skimmer firepower across a dense, interlocking threat web. The engine runs on Path of the Outcast's detection mechanic — Rangers and Shroud Runners force enemy units into extended detection range when selected to shoot, exposing hidden units and enabling the rest of the force to punish anything that tries to hide or screen safely, while Eldrad and stacked Warlocks amplify every activation with buffs. It thrives against armies that rely on obscured positioning or fragile screens, using layered lethal firepower to systematically strip units that cannot stay out of sight. Armies that can absorb the shooting attrition, close the distance quickly, or deny the shooting phase through alpha strike pressure crack this build open by collapsing the careful activation sequencing it depends on.
609: Built around Contemptor-Achillus and Contemptor-Galatus Dreadnoughts alongside Venerable Contemptors, Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Vertus Praetors, a Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike, and a Blade Champion, this list runs the Might of the Moritoi detachment to give every Walker +2" Movement plus bonuses to advance and charge rolls, turning its Dreadnought core into a rapid mid-table brawling force. The plan is to crash walkers and fast cavalry into priority threats early, using Shield Host's Ka'tah cycling to either fish for Critical Hits or improve Armour Penetration depending on the matchup, while tough infantry blobs hold objectives behind the assault. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that cannot reposition to avoid the incoming charge wave, as the threat range and volume of elite melee attacks overwhelm static defenses. Armies that can alpha-strike the Dreadnoughts before they engage, or screen the mid-table with expendable units to delay charges, can blunt the engine before it reaches full momentum.
540:
Built around Sanguinary Guard, Captains with Jump Packs, Commander Dante, and Vindicators, this list pairs an elite jump-infantry assault core with heavy demolisher firepower under the Angelic Inheritors detachment, using Angelic Legacy abilities — primarily Sanguinary Grace — to keep Characters mobile and aggressive after melee trades.

The engine is relentless pressure: Sanguinary Guard and jump-pack Characters crash into midfield while Vindicators blast blobs and armor from range, with Sanguinary Grace letting fallen-back Characters immediately shoot and charge again to sustain the grind.

It punishes infantry-dense and mid-tier armor lists that can't absorb simultaneous melee and demolisher-cannon pressure across multiple threat vectors.

Durable, high-model-count elite armies that shrug off blast damage and tarpit the jump units drain the list's momentum, as losing the assault-gunline synchronization leaves the Vindicators isolated and easy to screen out.
584: Built around Gaunt's Ghosts, Tempestus Scions with Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Krieg Combat Engineers, and layered heavy weapons platforms across Krieg, Cadian, and Catachan squads, all operating under Designation Force's Signal Flares from Scout Sentinels to paint targets. The plan is to use Signal Flares to mark enemy units, then drown them in stacked heavy weapon fire from multiple directions while Scions and Engineers threaten objectives and mid-board pressure forces the opponent to advance into prepared kill zones. This build punishes slow, durable elite armies that cluster together, where the sheer volume of coordinated gunline fire overwhelms layered saves before they can close. It cracks open against fast alpha-strike threats and deep-strike pressure that bypasses the screen entirely, forcing expensive elite infantry to absorb charges they were never designed to weather.
548: Built around Hellhounds, Rogal Dorn Commanders, Leman Russ Exterminators, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Hippogriff AFVs, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is a heavy armoured gunline running the Bridgehead Strike detachment, with about two-thirds of lists pairing it with Hammer of the Emperor for supercharged Squadron advances. The plan is to flood the board with durable, repair-sustained armour, grind down opposing units through overwhelming volume of tank fire, and use Battleline Scions in lists that include them to contest objectives while the vehicle core bleeds enemies dry. It punishes low-armour elite armies that struggle to crack multiple T10+ hulls per turn, especially when Enginseers keep key tanks topped up. However, truly elite anti-tank armies or high-mobility deep-strike threats can isolate and pick off individual tanks before the repair engine compensates, leaving the relatively slow gunline unable to redeploy in time.
610: Built around Blade Champions, Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, and Allarus Custodians, this is a dense, transport-heavy melee force that floods the midboard with elite infantry and refuses to let go of it. The win condition is controlling primary through sheer durability — near-unkillable gold-armoured bodies sitting on objectives while Blade Champions and Allarus Custodians punish anything that contests, with layered melee threat deterring would-be clearers. It excels against armies that rely on low-volume, high-damage shooting to remove mid-table infantry, since Custodes models simply absorb that punishment and keep scoring. It cracks open badly against mass-damage output or high-AP saturation that overwhelms individual-model toughness, and any list that can reliably deny melee engagement while stacking mortal wounds or psychic pressure will find the build short on answers.
542: Built around Chaos Rhinos ferrying Legionaries, Noise Marines, and Chosen into position, with Cultist Mobs screening, Chaos Bikers and Red Corsairs Raiders pressuring flanks, Huron Blackheart and a Chaos Lord buffing the midfield, and Defilers providing heavy fire support, all operating under Renegade Raiders. The plan is to advance and shoot from Rhinos or disembark onto objectives, where the detachment's Assault-weapon rule enables full salvos after moving and the AP+1 bonus near objectives turns every ranged attack into a harder punch against anything sitting on a marker. It punishes static gunline armies that cluster on objectives, because the AP improvement stacks with already-high-volume shooting to strip armor saves from entrenched infantry and vehicles alike. It cracks open under pressure from fast melee threats or deep-strike alpha strikes that pin Rhinos before they deploy their cargo, stranding key units out of position and negating the objective-proximity AP bonus entirely.
471: Built around Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, Knight Despoilers, War Dog Karnivores, and War Dog Stalkers running Infernal Lance, this is a Nurgle-flavoured big-knight hammer that uses cheap, disgusting objective chaff to hold ground while armoured killers do the work. The Infernal Lance's Malefic Surge Empowers knights to punch above their already considerable weight, with Karnivores and Stalkers hunting armour across every quadrant of the board. It punishes elite mechanised lists badly — layered anti-armour output overwhelms repair-style or low-model-count armies that can't absorb simultaneous threats from multiple massive chassis. Hordes of cheap bodies or alpha-strike lists that can strip the chaff screen early expose the knights' relatively low model count and force them onto objectives naked.
595: Built around Indomitor and Fortis Kill Teams, a Captain in Gravis Armour, Watch Master, Deathwatch Terminators, and Veterans, this Black Spear Task Force army floods the board with mixed-composition Kill Teams whose majority-Toughness wounding rule makes them deceptively durable against volume fire. The plan is to park bodies across every objective while the Kill Teams' flexible weapon loadouts — guided by the Tome of Ectoclades and Thief of Secrets enhancements — cycle the right tools into range to crack whatever target type the opponent presents. It punishes gunlines and horde armies particularly hard, bringing enough bodies and wound-dilution to weather attrition while returning fire across multiple threat profiles simultaneously. However, it struggles against concentrated elite melee lists that can isolate and delete Kill Teams before the majority-Toughness trick matters, and its relatively thin offensive ceiling means it rarely seizes decisive board swings against optimised alpha-strike builds.
570: Built around Mortarion, Defilers, Daemon Prince of Nurgle, Poxwalkers, Chaos Spawn, Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion and Virulence, and a Tallyman, this is a dense, multi-layered Virulent Vectorium army that locks down objectives through sheer attrition and sustained threat presence. The win condition is grinding the opponent into Contagion range, then stacking lethal firepower from Defilers and coordinated Characters to punish anything that contests, while Poxwalkers and Spawn screen and deny approach lanes. It punishes slow or low-mobility armies that cannot avoid Contagion range, where Mortarion and the Deathshroud become nearly impossible to shift from held objectives. However, fast alpha-strike lists that kill the screening layers early and isolate Mortarion before the Contagion bubble is established can crack the army open before its attrition engine ever fires.
539: Built around Rotigus, the Great Unclean One, Deathshroud Terminators, and a Lord of Contagion surrounded by waves of Beasts of Nurgle, Poxwalkers, Nurglings, and Plaguebearers, this is a Tallyband Summoners list that stacks Contagion Range bonuses by clustering Death Guard characters inside Plague Legions blobs to push the debuff aura as wide as possible across the board. The win condition is grinding opponents down through layered Nurgle's Gift lethality while burying objectives under disposable chaff that forces the enemy to chew through endless wounds before reaching the real threats. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count elite lists that struggle to clear the volume of bodies fast enough before Contagion effects compound into crippling debuffs. It cracks under fast, high-mobility armies that can isolate the key characters, collapse the 7" proximity bubbles, and strip the Contagion engine before the horde has time to absorb and redirect.
574: Built around Possessed, Chosen, Cultists, and Legionaries, this is a body-heavy infantry warband that floods the mid-table with durable, threatening units across multiple squad types. The plan is to overwhelm opponents through sheer volume of high-quality melee threats — Possessed and Chosen push into objectives while Cultists screen and contest, creating a layered advance that forces awkward prioritisation decisions. It punishes gun-line armies that lack the volume of fire to strip multiple tough infantry units simultaneously, as concentrated shooting gets absorbed by the horde while the real threats arrive intact. Armies that can tag and tie up Possessed early, or deliver a decisive alpha strike before the warband establishes board presence, expose the build's lack of a reliable single-source damage engine to dig out entrenched elite units.
575: Built around Lady Malys, Lelith Hesperax, Wyches, Hellions, Reavers, Incubi, and a swarm of Venoms and Raiders, this list layers Skysplinter Assault with Exhibition Of Slaughter to weaponize transport play across a mass of bodies. The engine is a coordinated disembark-and-charge sequence: units hopping off Venoms gain Ignores Cover on shooting and Lance in melee, while the Wych Cult tag grants Lethal Hits against everything that isn't a Monster or Vehicle, letting even chaff Wyches punch above their weight. It punishes slower mid-range armies that rely on cover saves and low model counts by flooding objectives with screening bodies and delivering multiple lethal combat threats simultaneously from multiple vectors. Armies with strong anti-horde shooting or durable Vehicles that shrug Exhibition Of Slaughter's Lethal Hits can thin the swarm faster than it scores, and anything that denies the disembark trigger—or locks Venoms in combat—collapses the kill chain.
541: Built around Raptors, Warp Talons, a jump pack Chaos Lord, Defilers, Chosen, and Cultist Mob screens, this is a mobile assault force that crashes into mid-board early and never lets up. The engine is attrition pressure: strip enemy units below half-strength to trigger battle-shock cascades — Nightmare Hunt forces extra tests on weakened squads while Murdertalon Raiders converts that shocked state into re-roll-hit offense and incoming -1 to hit defensively, creating a self-reinforcing kill spiral. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally, since landing even a few casualties triggers the battle-shock engine against small units that are structurally vulnerable to morale degradation. Dense horde armies and high-wound multi-wound infantry blunt the plan however, because killing to half-strength thresholds becomes expensive, the battle-shock chain stalls, and the list's mediocre shooting struggles to close the gap.
588: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Lord Exultants, Tormentors, Lucius, Defilers, winged Daemon Princes, and Fulgrim, this Peerless Bladesmen list is a charge-hungry melee swarm that layers Spectacle of Slaughter's Fights First onto Flawless Blades to threaten double-activation brawls in the mid-table. The engine is mass charging multiple units simultaneously — Peerless Bladesmen grants Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 to any unit that charged, turning every collision into a points-generating kill chain that snowballs scoring through raw body removal. It punishes elite infantry lists that can't absorb volume attacks across multiple threat vectors, especially when Lord Exultants buff nearby units and Defilers force awkward target-priority splits. However, heavy shooting lists that delete charging units before they connect, or anything with durable screens that slow the advance, can strip the tempo this build entirely depends on.
581: Built around Inquisitor Kroyle, multiple Subductor Squads, Imperial Navy Breachers, Deathwatch Kill Teams, Sisters of Battle with Immolators, Inquisitorial Agents, a Rogue Trader Entourage, Inquisitorial Chimeras, and supporting Inquisitors including Draxus, this is a high-volume Imperialis Fleet gunline that floods the board with cheap, varied infantry packed into transports. The win condition is leveraging the Eliminate At All Costs command phase ability to stack +1 to hit onto a priority threat while the sheer mass of bodies — often deep-struck via Combat Landers and positioned with Clandestine Operation — controls objectives and generates layered shooting across multiple fronts simultaneously. The list punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear through multiple waves of screens and objective-holders fast enough, drowning them in activations and sustained fire from skimmer-mounted platforms. It cracks under pressure from high-mobility alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete individual transport clusters before the infantry spreads out, or against armies with enough blast and area-damage to exploit the massed horde footprint.
592: Built around Castellan Crowe, multiple Purifier Squads, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, and Nemesis Dreadknights supported by Strike and Interceptor Squads, this list uses the Warpbane Task Force detachment to project Hallowed Ground across the battlefield by keeping Purifiers on mid-board objectives. The win condition is controlling No Man's Land early to unlock the detachment's third Hallowed Ground trigger, then layering lethal firepower from Dreadknights into whatever threatens that grip. It punishes horde armies and infantry-dense lists through massed, lethal-output shooting and combat across multiple bodies that are hard to shift from objectives. It cracks when opponents deny mid-board presence early, collapsing the Hallowed Ground engine before it activates and leaving the Dreadknight threat without the positional support it relies on.
591: Built around multiple Paladin Squads, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, Castellan Crowe, Grand Master Voldus, a Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight, Brotherhood Librarian, and Interceptor Squads, this list runs Argent Assault with the Banishers strat to flood the board with elite Psychic melee infantry across multiple angles. The engine is stacking Argent Assault's wound-roll bonus on Paladins swinging into high-Toughness targets while Banishers' Leadership test unlocks Sustained Hits 1 or additional melee output, turning every fight phase into a compounding kill chain that scores through threat saturation rather than careful positioning. It punishes mid-toughness elite armies that can't withstand multiple simultaneous melee engagements, as the sheer volume of Psychic melee attacks across many units overwhelms focused defensive screens. Armies that can alpha-strike a key Paladin brick early or neutralise the Banishers Leadership window with Battleshock pressure will blunt the fight-phase engine before it compounds.
594: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Armiger Helverins, and a Knight Destrier, this list plants two foundation objectives at game start to establish a defensive line and then floods that corridor with fast, hard-hitting Armiger chassis supported by Bondsman abilities that strip cover from every ranged attack. The win condition is controlling your foundations while the Helverins' autocannons erase entrenched infantry and vehicles at range, and the Warglaives threaten mobile flanking kills against anything that contests. It punishes slow, heavily armoured lists that rely on cover saves and clustered positioning, since layered Bondsman synergies make cover essentially irrelevant across the defensive line. Highly mobile elite armies that can split its activation economy, contest both foundations simultaneously, or survive the mid-range bracket with invulnerable saves will stretch this build thin and crack it open.
580: Built around paired Doomsday Arks, the Silent King, C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, Canoptek Wraiths, Flayed Ones, and Technomancers, this list plants a firebase of devastating long-range ark fire behind a layered melee screen of durable, self-repairing bodies. The plan is to force the opponent into a dilemma — crack the melee screen and walk into ark fire, or ignore the screen and lose board control to Wraiths and Flayed Ones pressuring objectives. It punishes slow or static gunlines that can't quickly clear durable screening units, letting the arks fire freely while Technomancers keep bodies on the table through reanimation support. It struggles against fast, high-volume anti-infantry lists that can strip screens in a single turn and then freely reposition to deny the arks viable targets while outrunning the build's reactive threat radius.
604: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses, Boyz, Trukks, and a supporting mass of Nobz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Stormboyz, and Breaka Boyz under the War Horde detachment, this list floods the table with cheap Gretchin screens and delivers wave after wave of melee infantry. The win condition is raw combat saturation — War Horde's Sustained Hits 1 on every Ork melee weapon means each charge generates more hits than the volume of bodies already implies, letting Ghazghkull and Warboss-buffed units delete priority targets while Trukks and Battlewagons deliver fresh threats faster than opponents can answer. It punishes elite low-model-count lists through sheer anti-tank overload and melee weight, overwhelming armies that can only deal with one or two threats per turn. It cracks open against armies that can shoot transports off the board at range before the Orks close, stranding infantry in the open and defanging the entire delivery mechanism.
601: Built around massed Boyz squads, Gretchin screens, Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Painboyz, Warbosses, Stormboyz, Kommandos, and Bigbosses, this is a wall-to-wall green tide that drowns the midboard in bodies. The win condition is melee attrition at scale — Ghazghkull and Warbosses amplify the mob, Painboyz keep key units fighting through casualties, and Sustained Hits 1 across all Ork melee weapons turns sheer volume of attacks into reliable damage output. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot efficiently clear 100+ wounds of infantry, forcing kill-point trades that favour the Ork player's raw replacement capacity. It cracks open against high-volume mortal wounds, blast weapons, or heavy indirect fire that farms hordes efficiently, since losing coherency in the Boyz blobs before they reach combat collapses the entire engine.
605: Built around Meganobz, Nobz, Warboss in Mega Armour, Warboss, Ghazghkull Thraka, and Battlewagons, this list is a wall of armoured Ork elites surging forward behind Trukks and Battlewagons, with Gretchin and Boyz flooding the midboard and Painboyz keeping the heavies alive. The engine is the Bully Boyz detachment's second Waaagh!, which lets the Warboss-heavy roster stack combat buffs twice per game, slamming Meganobz and Nobz into targets with amplified hitting power to grind out kill secondaries and contest objectives through attrition. It punishes elite-light armies that lack the volume of AP or high-damage output needed to chew through multiple waves of durable, buffed infantry before the second Waaagh! detonates. Armies with reliable high-AP mass shooting or strong fight-first mechanics crack it open by removing the Warbosses before the second Waaagh! fires, stripping the build of its core damage multiplier.
600: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, massed Boyz squads, multiple Warbosses, and a deep bench of Painboys keeping bodies on the table, this Freebooter Krew list drowns the board in Orks Infantry under the Sustained Hits 1 aura the detachment grants to every attack while a loot objective designation focuses the horde's momentum on a single high-value target each turn. The win condition is a rolling melee flood — Ghazghkull triggers the Waaagh!, Warbosses stack leadership pressure, and waves of Boyz crash objectives faster than the opponent can clear them while Kommandos and Wazdakka Gutsmek provide flanking threat and mobile disruption. It punishes low-model-count elite armies brutally, overwhelming their damage output with sheer attrition and Painboy healing that makes each squad far stickier than it looks. Hard volume-of-fire lists and anything with reliable blast weapons can gut a wave before it arrives, and losing Ghazghkull early collapses the Waaagh! engine the whole horde depends on.
602: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Wazdakka Gutsmek, mobs of Boyz and Gretchin screening, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Tankbustas, Lootas, and Flash Gitz all riding Trukks and flooding midboard, this is a Freebooter Krew horde that earns Sustained Hits 1 on every attack made by its Infantry, Mounted, and Walker units. The win condition is loot-objective control married to overwhelming volume of fire — Git-Spotter Squig sharpens shooting, Painboys keep blobs alive, and the Waaagh! layered with More Dakka! turns every ranged mob into a Sustained Hits 1, Assault-capable firehose that drowns opponents in dice. It punishes elite armies with low model counts by simply outscoring and outshooting them on the loot objective while their anti-horde output can't keep pace with the replenishment this wall of green provides. Armies that can pop Trukks at range before the Waaagh! activates, or deny midboard presence early with alpha-strike firepower, can collapse the momentum before Sustained Hits 1 comes fully online.
593: Built around Logan Grimnar, double squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, a Captain in Terminator Armour, and a supporting Terminator Assault Squad, this is a heavily armoured melee freight-train running Saga of the Great Wolf, cycling its Hunting Packs each Command phase to flex between aggressive charges and precise combat output. The plan is to deliver a dense terminator blob into the mid-table, brawl through anything holding objectives, and let Logan's command presence amplify the unit's already brutal close-range killing power. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't strip multi-wound armoured infantry fast enough before the wall arrives and locks them in combat. It cracks when faced with high-volume mortal wound output or elite shooting that can surgically delete key characters before the blob gets into position — Bjorn and Arjac are load-bearing damage multipliers, and losing either early bleeds combat threat hard.
598: Built around Biovores, Zoanthropes, a Neurotyrant, Raveners, Hormagaunts, Lictors, Neurolictors, The Red Terror, Hyperadapted Raveners, Trygon, The Swarmlord, and Tyranid Primes with Lash Whips, this Subterranean Assault list uses the Burrower keyword on Trygons and Mawlocs to threaten sudden underground emergence while a sprawling swarm of fast melee units and synapse controllers floods the midboard. The win condition is overwhelming positional coverage — Lictors and Neurolictors infiltrate to deny deployment and set up charges, Raveners and Hormagaunts contest objectives early, and Burrowing Trygons (frequently upgraded to Trygon Prime) punch through backlines to collapse scoring late. It punishes static, spread-thin gunlines that can't clear multiple simultaneous threats across the whole board, especially when layered mortal-wound output from Zoanthropes and Biovores softens screens before the melee wave arrives. However, lists built around elite low-drop armies with dense anti-horde firepower can surgically strip the cheap objective holders before the underground threats emerge, leaving the swarm without board presence when it matters most.
607: Built around Magnus the Red, wall-to-wall Rubric Marines (nearly three squads deep), Scarab Occult Terminators, Sekhetar Robots, and a support web of Sorcerers and Infernal Masters, all running Grand Coven to cycle through three one-shot psychic empowerment abilities across the game. The plan is to blanket the board with bodies — Tzaangors and Rhino-mounted Rubrics holding ground while Magnus and Daemon Princes apply elite kill pressure — then time the Grand Coven pulses (range extension, then mortal-wound output) to spike damage in the turns that matter most. It punishes low-model-count armies brutally, using sheer objective saturation and layered psychic lethality to overwhelm lists that cannot clear hordes efficiently. Concentrated high-damage shooting or elite melee that can isolate and delete Magnus early cracks the list open, since the empowerment engine and kill threat both collapse without him.
485: Built around Norn Emissaries, Norn Assimilators, Tyrannofexes, Maleceptors, Exocrines, Biovores, the Hive Tyrant, and the Swarmlord, this is a wall of Monsters operating under Crusher Stampede and the Talons of the Norn Queen, giving the Norn constructs their Protean Purpose adaptability on top of the detachment's bonus Hit and Wound rolls as units take damage. The win condition is objective control through sheer Monster bulk — healthy units sitting on objectives gain +2 OC while the long-range firepower of Tyrannofexes and Exocrines strips opposing holders, and damaged Monsters actually hit and wound harder, turning attrition into a threat. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot project enough bodies to contest multiple objectives simultaneously against high-OC, high-durability targets. Horde screens and volume anti-tank crack it open by bypassing the OC engine and overwhelming individual Monsters before the wounded-Monster hit-and-wound bonuses can compensate.
565: Built around Exalted Eightbound, Slaughterbound, Eightbound, Jakhals, Defilers, Daemon Princes, and Forgefiends under the Brazen Engines detachment, this is a wall of daemon vehicles and frenzied infantry that smashes into the midboard and refuses to leave. The win condition is attrition-through-aggression: Terror of Khorne battle-shocks units engaged with daemon vehicles, softening combat resolution while Slaughterbound and Eightbound grind through whatever survives, with Jakhals screening and contesting objectives to keep the scoring engine ticking. It punishes elite melee armies and low-model-count lists that can't outlast the layered lethality of multiple hard-hitting units arriving in waves, while Forgefiends and Defilers provide mobile anti-armour to deny vehicle-heavy gunlines safe distance. Lists that can kite, consistently shoot the Jakhals screen off the board early, and deny the close-range engagement entirely will starve this build of both its combat triggers and its board presence before it can establish dominance.
655:
Built around Warlock Skyrunners, Eldrad Ulthran, War Walkers, and Rangers, this list leans hard into the Armoured Warhost detachment, giving every Aeldari Vehicle unit the Assault ability so they can advance and still put out full firepower.

The engine is layered vehicle shooting — War Walkers and Fire Prisms push up aggressively each turn while Warlock Skyrunners provide psychic support, with Rangers locking down backfield objectives to free the vehicles to dictate range.

It punishes slow, static armies that can't reposition to avoid concentrated fire, overwhelming them with sustained mobile shooting before they can respond.

Its weakness is high-volume mortal-wound output and dedicated anti-tank overload — strip the vehicles fast and the list's scoring engine collapses, as the infantry core is too light to hold ground independently.
712: Built around Witchseekers, Prosecutors, Vigilators, Custodian Guard, Allarus Custodians, and Anathema Psykana Rhinos, this list floods the mid-table with Sisters of Silence infantry delivered in transports, backed by elite Custodes muscle. The win condition is sustained mid-board brawling — Sisters units screen, contest, and nullify threats while Custodian Guard and Allarus Custodians grind through opposing melee pieces to dominate scoring zones. Detachments like Lions of the Emperor reward aggressive isolation play by adding +1 to Hit and Wound when units operate away from friendly models, making individual squads punching well above their points. Anything that can strip transports early or deny the mid-table foothold — massed anti-infantry shooting or fast alpha-strike threats — forces the Sisters infantry to foot-slog, collapsing the tempo the whole engine depends on.
719: Built around Repentia Squads, Arco-Flagellants, Celestian Sacresants, and Morvenn Vahl, this Penitent Host list is a mobile melee swarm that rotates Vows of Atonement each round — pushing Penitent units an extra 3" or converting fight-phase triggers into compounding damage output. The win condition is delivering multiple high-volume melee units simultaneously into priority targets, with Hospitallers and the Triumph of Saint Katherine sustaining bodies on objectives while the Sacresants' boosted WS from Sacred Champions turns elite combatants into reliable killers. It punishes armies that rely on a single defensive screen or small elite model counts, flooding the fight phase with redundant threats faster than point-for-point efficient trading can answer. It cracks open when faced with strong shooting denial, deep strike lockout, or armies that kill transports early and strand slow melee infantry short of contact range.
