710: Built around a wall of Custodes Dreadnoughts — Contemptor-Achillus, Contemptor-Galatus, Telemon, and Venerable Contemptors — supported by Witchseekers and Caladius Grav-Tanks, this is a mid-table brawler that uses the Solar Spearhead's OC+2 bonus on full-strength vehicles to physically dominate objectives while its guns work. The win condition is simple brutality: park Telemons and Galatus Contemptors at full strength on key points to spike OC to threatening levels, then use Achillus and Caladius to eliminate whatever tries to contest. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't generate enough bodies to trade OC or crack multiple durable, high-toughness vehicles simultaneously. However, horde lists and anything generating mass volume of attacks can chip vehicles below Starting Strength before they score, collapsing the OC engine and forcing a damage-output race the list struggles to win efficiently.
709: Built around Allarus Custodians, Shield-Captains in Allarus Terminator Armour, and a walker core of Contemptor-Achillus, Contemptor-Galatus, and Telemon Dreadnoughts, this list runs Lions Of The Emperor to squeeze +1 Hit and +1 Wound on isolated units, and Might Of The Moritoi to push its Walkers up the board faster with enhanced Move, advance, and charge rolls. The plan is to crash an elite terminator-and-walker brick into the midboard, isolate individual units to trigger the Lions buff, and grind opponents off objectives through sheer melee durability and output. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that cannot screen the midboard, where the Walker mobility upgrades let Dreadnoughts reach combat before the opponent can react. Dense horde screens or shooting armies that can flood the 6" Lions bubble with cheap bodies will dilute the hit-and-wound bonuses and blunt the brick's damage output before it reaches combat.
547: Built around Tech-Priest Enginseers keeping multiple Titanic engines operational, Scout Sentinels screening the advance, Lord Solar Leontus coordinating the column, and a rotating core of Baneblade, Banesword, and Stormsword super-heavies, this is a Steel Hammer gunline that fields the heaviest armour the Imperium can muster. The win condition is overwhelming firepower at range — the Banesword and Stormsword lob apocalyptic ordnance into clustered targets while the Baneblade mops up whatever survives, with Steel Hammer's ability letting Titanic and Squadron units shoot into Engagement Range so screens cannot simply walk up and hug them into irrelevance. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to kill multiple Titanic targets per turn before the Enginseers restore wounds. Swarm lists or anything that can flood the table and tie up multiple super-heavies simultaneously stretches repair resources thin and buries the army in chip damage it cannot outpace.
711: Built around Venatari Custodians, Allarus Custodians, a Blade Champion, Custodian Guard, Vertus Praetors, a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, Custodian Wardens, and Witchseekers, this is a densely packed elite infantry force running primarily Shield Host with Tharanatoi Hammerblow layered on top — using ingress moves to land Terminators into combat with re-rollable charges. The plan is to dominate the midboard through physical presence, using the Ka'tah system's Critical Hit and AP improvements to punch through armour while Venatari and Praetors provide mobile threat vectors that stretch the opponent thin. It punishes slower, lower-mobility armies that can't contest the midboard early, overwhelming them with durable multi-wound bodies that demand more resources to remove than most lists can sustain. Concentrated high-AP shooting, volume anti-infantry overload, or deep strike denial tools that keep Terminators off their ingress angles crack this build before its melee engine fully engages.
717: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Celestian Sacresants, and a broad supporting cast of Canonesses, Palatines, Immolators, Arco-Flagellants, and Castigators, this list runs the Hallowed Martyrs detachment, which rewards units for taking casualties by granting bonus Hit rolls when below Starting Strength and bonus Wound rolls when Below Half-strength. The plan is to deliberately feed units into combat, let them degrade, then unleash enhanced offensive output from wounded squads while Hospitallars and the Saintly Example enhancement keep key models alive just long enough to maximise that damage window. It punishes lists that deal incremental chip damage — precisely the kind of attrition that would normally suppress a force instead triggers the detachment's cascading hit-and-wound bonuses across a wide toolbox of mobile infantry and armour. However, lists that can delete entire units outright before they degrade, or that simply overwhelm the army's modest durability with concentrated high-volume fire, deny the martyrdom engine entirely and leave this force performing below par.
706: Built around Vertus Praetors, Shield-Captains on Dawneagle Jetbikes, Allarus Custodians, Allarus-armoured Shield-Captains, Telemon Heavy Dreadnoughts, and Witchseekers, this list runs the Lions Of The Emperor detachment to turn every isolated unit into a precision killing machine — +1 to hit and +1 to wound whenever no friendly unit sits within 6", rewarding a spread, skirmishing deployment over tight castle play. The win condition is mid-board dominance: fast jetbike units claim and contest objectives early while Allarus deep strikers and Telemons — boosted by Might Of The Moritoi's +2" Move and charge bonus — hit flanks hard enough to force opponents off scoring positions. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally, since the Lions bonus stacks with already-elite statlines to delete individual high-value units without needing volume. Dense horde screens and armies that can flood the 6" bubble consistently dilute the detachment bonus and bog down the relatively low model count.
662: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, and Gaunt's Ghosts, with Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Krieg Combat Engineers, and Cadian Shock Troops filling out the board, this Bridgehead Strike list deep strikes elite infantry onto objectives and blasts everything in sight the moment boots hit the ground. The engine is the Bridgehead Strike detachment rule: units that arrive from reserves shoot at +1 to hit, so Command Squads and Scions drop directly into scoring position and immediately dump high-volume, accurate firepower into priority targets. It punishes slow, high-toughness gunline armies that can't react to mid-board drops, overwhelming them with mobile anti-armour and massed bodies claiming Battleline objectives. Resilient melee armies that can weather the alpha strike and lock the Scions in Engagement Range before they shoot again dismantle this list, since its defensive profile is paper-thin once the drop turn passes.
661: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Cadian Shock Troops, Kasrkin, Krieg Combat Engineers, Death Riders, Taurox transports, Rogal Dorn Commanders, Cadian Command Squads, and Gaunt's Ghosts, this Grizzled Company list floods the table with ordered infantry and mobile firepower — the detachment's ability to stack extra Orders on every officer means nearly every unit rerolls hit rolls of 1 simultaneously. The plan is to drown opponents in volume, using Taurox-mounted Scions and Death Riders for mobile anti-armour pressure while stationary gunlines and horde infantry lock down objectives. It punishes low-durability elite armies that can't withstand sustained, army-wide reroll-buffed fire across multiple fronts. Opponents with strong alpha-strike capability or long-range mortal-wound output can strip key officers early, collapsing the Order chain and gutting the reroll engine before it fully fires.
691: Built around the Emperor's Champion, Assault Intercessors, Crusader Squads, Intercessors, Sword Brethren, Marshals, Castellans, Scouts, and Repulsor Executioners, this Bastion Task Force list floods the board with Adeptus Astartes Battleline infantry backed by heavy skimmer firepower. The core engine exploits the detachment's ability to shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back, keeping Battleline units perpetually active while Repulsor Executioners hammer armour from range and infantry swarm objectives without sacrificing action economy. It punishes slower, lower-model-count lists that can't match the volume of bodies, combining anti-tank overload from the Repulsors with mass Battleline pressure to overwhelm positional defenses. It struggles against armies that can strip infantry efficiently at range before the advance closes, and lists with durable elite melee threats that neutralise the Battleline swarm before it can dictate the combat phase.
643: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, a Captain with Jump Pack, Chaplain with Jump Pack, and Commander Dante, this is a jump-heavy melee assault force supplemented by Baal Predators, Scouts, and Intercessors holding ground. The win condition is crashing buffed jump infantry into priority targets — Dante and the Chaplain elevating Death Company and Sanguinary Guard into elite-killing threats while Baal Predators provide mobile anti-armour fire support to crack vehicles that melee can't efficiently reach. It punishes armies with exposed elite infantry and light vehicles, using high-mobility charges to isolate and delete key pieces before the opponent can consolidate their position. It struggles against tight screening, durable gunlines, and anything that can weather the initial assault wave and grind back, since the list lacks the resilience to sustain prolonged attrition fights.
692: Built around Repulsor Executioners, High Marshal Helbrecht, the Emperor's Champion, and a Land Raider Redeemer ferrying assault infantry, this is a Ceramite Sentinels gunline that plays terrain as a force multiplier — units entrenched in cover re-roll 1s to hit and wound, turning static fire positions into premium shooting platforms. The plan is to park Repulsor Executioners and infantry inside terrain features early, grind out damage with sustained re-rolls while Helbrecht and the Champion push threat vectors forward, and use jump-pack assault intercessors to contest or punish overextension. It punishes mobile anti-tank overload lists that need to trade efficiently, because the re-roll economy makes every shooting phase more reliable and attrition-heavy. Aggressive alpha-strike armies that can deny terrain occupation on turn one — or simply flood the board before the Entrenched bubble activates — expose how dependent this list is on its setup conditions.
693: Built around Crusade Ancients, Crusader Squads, Sword Brethren, Bladeguard Veterans, Chaplain Grimaldus, and Chaplains — all backed by Repulsor Executioners and Execrators — this Vindication Task Force list plays a layered gunline where Ancient units holding objectives gain wound-roll protection against high-Strength attacks, turning them into durable objective anchors rather than fragile banners. The win condition is attrition: Crusader Squads surge toward objectives while the Repulsor Executioners and Execrators project heavy skimmer firepower to clear threats, with Chaplains providing the Wrathful Procession's 5+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks to keep them alive. It punishes armies that rely on elite, high-Strength firepower to crack objectives, since the Ancient bubble actively degrades wound rolls against those attacks. It cracks under weight-of-fire from low-Strength, high-volume shooting that ignores the wound modifier entirely, or mobile armies that contest objectives before the gunline can stabilize.
694: Built around multiple Repulsor Executioners, Sword Brethren, Techmarines, Castellans, Marshals, and the Emperor's Champion, this is a mechanised Black Templars list running Ironstorm Spearhead to squeeze re-rolls from every Adeptus Astartes unit once per phase across hit, wound, or damage rolls. The plan is to park a heavy gunline of skimmer tanks on or behind objectives, use Sword Brethren transported inside Repulsors to threaten midfield, and grind scoring through sustained firepower while the Emperor's Champion punches elite units off priority targets. It punishes slower armour-heavy lists that can't contest volume fire from multiple Executioners simultaneously, each independently re-rolling key dice to maximise damage output. It cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike builds that can tag the Repulsors early, stranding the Sword Brethren and collapsing both the transport engine and the melee threat in one go.
645: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Vindicators, Commander Dante, and Death Company Marines with jump packs, this list pairs fast-moving elite infantry with heavy armoured firepower across multiple detachments — most commonly Rage-Cursed Onslaught for melee punch, but also Stormlance Task Force or Legacy of Grace in a significant minority of lists. The plan is to blast open armour and dense infantry with Vindicator shells while Sanguinary Guard and Death Company threaten midboard objectives, forcing opponents to split attention between the gunline and airborne melee pressure. It punishes slow, high-toughness armies by overloading them with mobile anti-armour and re-rolling wound rolls on melee attacks, while Scouts and Incursors screen objectives cheaply. Lists that can shut down the Vindicators at range and survive the initial charge threat — particularly those with strong anti-air or deep-strike denial screens — expose the relatively thin backfield and leave the melee elements isolated.
707: Built around Vertus Praetors, Shield-Captains on Dawneagle Jetbikes, a Telemon Heavy Dreadnought, Allarus Custodians, and Custodian Guard, this list runs the Might of the Moritoi and Shield Host detachments — pushing its Walker up the board faster while cycling Ka'tah selections to shift between Critical Hit generation and improved Armour Penetration across its elite melee core. The plan is to flood mid-table with high-durability bodies, use the jetbike units to contest and threaten simultaneously, and let the Telemon's boosted movement punch into whatever needs removing each turn. It punishes elite low-model-count lists that can't trade efficiently into near-unkillable individual models, bleeding them dry on points through relentless mid-board presence. Volume shooting and high-AP ranged armies that can strip wounds before the charge land are the primary threat, as the list's scoring engine collapses if the expensive infantry never make contact.
667: Built around Bloodcrushers, Lords of Change, Be'lakor, Bloodthirsters, Screamers, and Cultist Mob screens, this list runs the Cavalcade of Chaos detachment to enable its LEGIONES DAEMONICA MOUNTED units to fall back and still shoot and charge — turning every engagement into a no-commitment threat that the opponent can never truly lock down. The win condition is layered attrition and mobility dominance: Bloodcrushers and Screamers harass and fall back freely, Lords of Change project ranged pressure, and Be'lakor enables shadow-play disruption while the whole engine bleeds opponents off objectives. It punishes slower, melee-committed armies that rely on locking units in combat to neutralize them, since the fall-back-and-charge loop simply ignores that trade entirely. It cracks open against elite shooting armies that can delete mounted units before they disengage, removing the engine that makes the detachment's core mechanic matter.
666:
Built around Rotigus, multiple Great Unclean Ones, dense Plaguebearer blobs, Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, and Sloppity Bilepipers, this is a suffocating Nurgle horde that floods the board with cheap, disgustingly resilient bodies backed by monstrous anchor pieces.

The plan is to drown opponents in attrition — parking Plaguebearers and Nurglings on objectives while Beasts of Nurgle and Great Unclean Ones grind through anything that tries to contest, squeezing points from a board state the opponent simply cannot clear fast enough.

It punishes low-volume shooting and combat-light lists brutally, as nothing in those armies can chew through the sheer number of wounds fast enough to deny scoring.

High-damage, high-volume anti-horde firepower cracks it open — lists that can efficiently delete full squads per turn will outpace the regeneration and leave objectives naked before the horde can reinforce.
668: Built around Screamers, Lords of Change, Flamers, Kairos Fateweaver, Pink Horrors, and Be'lakor, this list runs Scintillating Legion with Warptide as a secondary detachment, combining a flexible toolkit of fast, lethal Tzeentch daemons with a mobile horde that can advance-and-still-shoot or charge. The engine is Flux token re-rolls stacked on critical Flamers shooting and Screamer sweeps, using Kairos and Lords of Change as command-and-control multipliers while Pink Horrors screen mid-board objectives and Warptide lets Battleline units advance without sacrificing their threat range. It punishes elite low-model armies that cannot answer simultaneous air, ground, and horde pressure across multiple threat vectors. It struggles against lists that can strip screens efficiently and then spike damage into the Lords of Change before Flux tokens can bail out the key rolls.
664: Built around Bloodcrushers, Flesh Hounds, and a Rendmaster on Blood Throne as the mounted Khorne strike force, supported by Beasts of Nurgle, Plaguebearers, Nurglings, a Great Unclean One, Skullmaster, and Be'lakor, this list runs Cavalcade of Chaos to let its LEGIONES DAEMONICA MOUNTED units fall back and still charge, keeping the kill engine perpetually engaged. The plan is to crash Bloodcrushers and Flesh Hounds into the midboard repeatedly — falling back out of unfavorable combats and immediately re-declaring charges — while Nurgle bodies and Nurglings clog objectives and drain opponent resources through attrition. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot replace bodies fast enough to survive repeated mounted charges cycling in and out of combat every turn. Horde lists that can flood the midboard and tar-pit the cavalry in place, denying the fall-back-and-charge loop, expose how dependent this build is on that single mechanical interaction to generate kills.
665: Built around Be'lakor, a Bloodthirster, Bloodmaster-led Bloodletters, Plaguebearers, Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, and waves of Cultist Mob infantry, this is a Shadow Legion horde that floods the board with layered, hard-to-shift bodies while hunting with elite killers. The win condition is threat saturation — Warptide lets Battleline units advance and still charge, so Bloodletters and Plaguebearers crash into combat the same turn they surge forward, while Be'lakor and the Bloodthirster peel apart anything that tries to hold the midfield anchor. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that cannot generate enough attacks to clear the sheer volume of wounds, especially when Nurglings and Beasts of Nurgle clog key lanes. However, high-volume lethal-hit shooting that reaches into multiple units simultaneously can outpace its regeneration and collapse the horde before the charge engine ever fires.
653: Built around Vashtorr the Arkifane, multiple Venomcrawlers, Defilers, and Warpsmiths backed by Cultist screens, this is a daemon vehicle swarm that leans primarily on the Soulforged Warpack detachment to power up Dark Pacts — letting its Heretic Astartes Daemon Vehicles invoke their contracts, gaining +1 to wound on ranged attacks and +2 Attacks in melee simultaneously. The win condition is overwhelming mobile anti-armour pressure: Venomcrawlers and Defilers make pacted attacks that punch far above their points cost, while Vashtorr and Warpsmiths keep the machine spirits churning and screens hold primary. It punishes armour-heavy and monster-dense lists brutally, where the layered lethality of buffed melee and ranged in the same activation creates anti-tank overload no single defensive layer can answer. However, elite infantry flooding the midboard with high-volume, low-Strength shooting can whittle the relatively fragile daemon vehicles before they Pact, and losing even one or two vehicles early collapses the output engine fast.
647: Built around Abaddon the Despoiler, Huron Blackheart, Chosen, Defilers, and waves of Cultist Mobs operating under Pactbound Zealots, this list marries a bloated horde screen to heavy walking firepower and elite melee threat. The engine is Pactbound Zealots' lethal hits on 5+ in melee, letting Abaddon and Chosen tear through armoured targets while Defilers suppress midfield and Cultists flood objectives to generate secondary points and deny deepstrike lanes. It punishes slow gunlines that can't clear bodies fast enough — the sheer volume of Cultists and Red Corsairs Raiders absorbs attrition while the elite hammer units close safely behind. Armies that can blast the screen early and isolate Abaddon or Chosen before they engage will crack the kill chain wide open.
470: Built around War Dog Karnivores, Brigands, and Stalkers flooding the board with fast medium walkers, screened by Cultist Mobs providing cheap bodies to contest and absorb damage. The plan is sheer volume — dozens of War Dog activations grind through opposing armies piece by piece, with Houndpack Lance's Sustained Hits 1 focusing firepower to efficiently delete priority targets each turn while Cultists hold backfield secondaries. It punishes low-model-count elite armies and heavy armour lists that can't trade efficiently against ten-plus activations of mobile anti-tank. However, it cracks against anything with high-volume, high-AP shooting that can strip War Dogs faster than they can cycle through objectives, since the individual chassis are durable but not resilient against anti-armour overload.
649: Built around Huron Blackheart, Chosen, Cultist Mobs, Masters of the Maelstrom, Defilers, Red Corsairs Raiders, and Cypher, this is a mass-horde gunline that floods the board with cheap bodies and hits surprisingly hard across multiple ranges. The plan is to drown opponents in volume — Cultists and Raiders hold and contest objectives while Chosen and Defilers punch into whatever threatens the midfield, with Huron and Masters of the Maelstrom providing command support to keep the machine running. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear waves of Cultists efficiently, trading up on resources while Defilers apply mid-table anti-armour pressure. It cracks when faced with high-AP mass damage that strips Cultist screens early, exposing the more expensive pieces to focus fire before they can engage on favorable terms.
635: Built around Land Speeder Vengances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Azrael, Deathwing Knights, and Scout and Intercessor Squads, this is a Darkflight Pursuit skimmer swarm that floods the board with fast, hard-hitting flyers. The win condition is Ignores Cover firepower from RAVENWING FLY units stripping entrenched infantry and armour off objectives while Deathwing Knights bodyblock and contest with their bulk. It punishes castle-style gunlines and fortified objective holders hard, since cover-dependent defensive positioning provides no protection against the detachment's ranged attacks. The vulnerability is volume anti-tank from mobile opponents — the speeders are fragile for their points, and losing two or three early collapses the damage output before Deathwing Knights can compensate in melee.
652: Built around Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Cultist Mobs, Red Corsairs Raiders, Abaddon the Despoiler, and Kravek Morne operating under the Pactbound Zealots detachment, this list blends daemon engines, transported infantry, and named character muscle into a mobile, multi-threat force. The win condition is anti-armour pressure at range and mid-table melee dominance — Defilers and Venomcrawlers threaten vehicles and monsters while Cultists ferry through Raiders to flood objectives, with Abaddon's and Kravek's melee punch closing out contested zones. Lethal Hits on unmodified 5s in melee rewards volume attacks, punishing armies that rely on durable multi-wound infantry blobs or lightly armoured hordes that can't trade back efficiently. The build cracks under elite, high-damage alpha strikes that delete daemon engines before they engage, stripping the anti-armour backbone and leaving the cultist screen overexposed.
638: Built around Ravenwing Black Knights, Ravenwing Command Squads, Outrider Squads, Land Speeder Vengeances, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Land Speeders, this is a hyper-mobile Dark Angels cavalry and skimmer force running Company of Hunters — which lets every Adeptus Astartes unit shoot after Advancing or Falling Back, and lets Mounted units also charge after doing so. The engine is relentless pressure: the entire army repositions freely each turn without sacrificing firepower or combat eligibility, flooding mid-table objectives while Land Speeder Vengeances and Thunderstrikes pump out mobile anti-armour from wherever they're needed. It punishes slow, static gunlines and transport-heavy infantry lists that rely on positional safety, since nothing in this army is ever out of range for long. Anything that can force it into a single decisive engagement — dense terrain limiting advance lanes or high-volume anti-tank that can strip skimmers before they reposition — exposes how fragile the individual units are when caught standing still.
648: Built around Huron Blackheart, near-ubiquitous Defilers, Warp Talons, Chosen, Masters of the Maelstrom, and waves of Cultist Mob and Red Corsairs Raiders screening forward, this list runs the Murdertalon Raiders detachment to weaponize its flying infantry against wounded or battle-shocked targets. The game plan is to stack pressure across the whole board — Defilers and the gunline grind enemy units below half-strength, then the Warp Talons and Chosen pile in with re-rolled hit rolls and -1 to-hit protection, while Veterans of the Long War focus-of-hatred stacking lets Huron's full force punch through a priority target in a single activation. It punishes elite low-model-count armies hard, where the horde screens objectives and the anti-armour engine repeatedly trips the half-strength threshold to unlock cascading bonuses. Armies that can alpha-strike the Warp Talons before they engage, or suppress the Defilers at range before half-strength triggers come online, strip out the core kill chain and leave the horde holding ground without enough teeth to close games.
640:
Built around Inner Circle Companions, multiple Librarians (including Terminator-armoured variants), Azrael, and Deathwing Knights, this is a dense Terminator-and-elite infantry list running Inner Circle Task Force with Librarius Conclave layered on top for round-by-round Psychic Discipline buffing.

The engine is Vowed objective manipulation: flip to Aggressive Push to threaten multiple uncontrolled markers simultaneously, then snap back to Defensive Footing to lock down a key hold, while Librarius Conclave rotates Divination or Biomancy onto whichever elite brick needs re-rolls or extra movement to execute the scoring swing.

It punishes slow, durable gunlines that can't clear tough Terminator bodies fast enough, leveraging layered lethality and transport-delivered infantry to overwhelm static defensive setups.

It cracks open against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete elite squads before the Vowed objective engine gets rolling, since losing one expensive brick early collapses both the scoring and the threat density simultaneously.
626: Built around Poxwalkers in mass, Plague Marines in Rhinos, Typhus, Deathshroud Terminators, a Lord of Contagion, Malignant Plaguecasters, a Tallyman, and a Biologus Putrifier, this build floods the table with diseased bodies across multiple detachment configurations — Paragons of Putrescence, Shamblerot Vectorium, Flyblown Host, and Death Lord's Chosen all appear, each layering a different contagion pressure vector. The win condition is Affliction stacking: blanket the board in Contagion Range, infect enemy units, then grind scoring through attrition while Deathshroud and Plague Marines in transports punch for kills. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally — the combination of mortal wound triggers, Poxwalker board saturation, and layered lethal threat overloads resilient single-unit targets. Armies that can outrange the Contagion envelope, deny the mid-table early, or blast through the Rhinos before Plague Marines embed crack the engine wide open.
641: Built around Inner Circle Companions, Azrael, multiple Librarians (including Terminator-armoured variants), Sternguard Veterans, Deathwing Knights, Intercessors, and a Lieutenant with combi-weapon, this is a dense, transport-heavy elite infantry hammer running the Librarius Conclave to flex Psychic Disciplines — Divination for rerolls on the kill turn, Biomancy for threat-range extension — across its psyker-heavy core. The plan is to deliver Deathwing Knights and Inner Circle Companions into close-quarters contact while Sternguard lay down concentrated mid-range firepower, with Azrael's aura amplifying both halves of the equation and the Fusillade enhancement (three-quarters of lists) sharpening the shooting spike. It punishes horde armies hard — the combination of volume elite melee and enhanced gunline output can strip cheap screening units before they deny space. However, the build struggles against fast alpha-strike armies that can strip Azrael early or avoid the kill-box entirely, collapsing the reroll and aura support the entire engine depends on.
627: Built around Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Poxwalkers, Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Mortarion, Typhus, Foetid Bloat-Drones, Chaos Spawn, and Daemon Princes of Nurgle running Virulent Vectorium, this is a wall of Lethal Hits pressure backed by durable bodies across every part of the board. The win condition is sticky objective control — Virulent Vectorium locks down markers once seized, so the plan is to plant Poxwalkers and Chaos Spawn on objectives early, then use Deathshroud and Lords of Contagion to make those positions punishing to contest. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to outmass the screening layers and cannot generate enough attacks to clear Lethal-boosted units efficiently. However, high-volume, long-range gunlines can chip through the slow advance before it reaches scoring positions, and the list's lack of speed means alpha-strike lists can seize objectives and bank points before the wall arrives.
537: Built around Poxwalkers, Plague Marines, Malignant Plaguecasters, Lords of Contagion, Deathshroud Terminators, Tallymen, Biologus Putrifiers, and Chaos Rhinos, this is a mid-board contagion-stacking army that uses the Champions Of Contagion detachment to cycle between Nurgle's plagues each battle round, with Paragons Of Putrescence extending Death Guard Character contagion ranges by 3" to flood the midfield with overlapping plague auras. The win condition is layered lethality: Malignant Plaguecasters and Lords of Contagion push contagion bubbles forward while Rhino-mounted Plague Marines and Deathshroud contest objectives, converting sustained plague exposure into attrition kills that grind opponents off the board. It punishes durable infantry-heavy lists that have to fight through the midfield, where stacked plague effects and Biologus Putrifier synergies reward slugging matches. It cracks open against fast, ranged armies that can strip characters from distance before contagion ranges come online, collapsing the aura engine before it reaches critical mass.
451: Built around Ravagers, Venoms, Scourges with heavy weapons, Archons, Incubi, Wyches, Drazhar, Lady Malys, Mandrakes, and Kabalite Warriors, this list floods the board with skimmer-mounted infantry and overlapping firepower across Exhibition Of Slaughter and Skysplinter Assault detachments. The win condition is punishing disembark windows — units hopping off Venoms and Raiders gain Ignores Cover on ranged weapons and Lance on melee, while Wych Cult units like Wyches and Incubi stack Lethal Hits against non-vehicles to shred infantry in the same turn they land. It brutalises horde armies and lightly armoured midfield holders that can't survive layered Lethal Hits melee combined with skimmer shooting. Durable elite armies with high saves or strong screening punish it back, as the fragile transport chassis die quickly under focused anti-tank fire and the entire threat engine collapses.
596: Built around massed Librarians (often two, including one in Terminator armour), Deathwatch Veterans, Indomitor Kill Teams, Deathwatch Terminator Squads, and Sternguard Veterans under the Bastion Task Force detachment, this is a heavy gunline that floods the board with Adeptus Astartes Battleline units that can shoot, charge, and perform Actions after Advancing or Falling Back. The win condition is sustained fire volume — Battleline units trigger a debuff on any enemy unit they hit, while the Librarius Conclave cycles Divination for re-rolls or Pyromancy to amplify shooting output every round, keeping damage consistent across multiple phases. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't weather repeated high-AP volleys and struggle to contest objectives against infantry that remains fully functional after repositioning. Horde armies that can absorb firepower and flood scoring zones, or deep-strike threats that force the gunline to split attention before it settles, crack this list open by overwhelming its relatively modest melee threat and forcing unfavorable reactive movement.
625: Built around Plague Marines and Poxwalkers screened forward in Chaos Rhinos, supported by Malignant Plaguecasters, a Lord of Contagion, Tallyman, Daemon Prince of Nurgle, Deathshroud Terminators, Biologus Putrifier, and Blightlord Terminators, this is a suffocating attrition list running the Virulent Vectorium detachment. The win condition is objective lockdown — once a Death Guard unit claims a marker, the detachment's sticky-objective rule means the opponent must physically overpower your presence to dislodge it, letting the list farm points while grinding enemies down through layered lethal damage output. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that can't mass enough bodies to contest multiple objectives simultaneously against durable, lethal infantry. It cracks open against fast, high-volume shooting armies that can clear the holding units before they absorb enough attacks, and against anything that reliably bypasses toughness and damage reduction at range.
654: Built around Lady Malys, Drazhar, Incubi, Wyches, Reavers, Mandrakes, and a swarm of Venoms and Raiders, this list runs Skysplinter Assault paired with Exhibition of Slaughter to stack disembark buffs onto a mass of cheap, fast bodies. The engine is delivering Incubi and Wyches out of Venoms with Ignores Cover on their shooting and Lance on their melee, while Wych Cult units trigger Lethal Hits against non-Monsters and non-Vehicles to shred infantry and light chaff at scale. It punishes objective-camping infantry hordes brutally — the layered Lethal Hits and Lance combination makes even defended midboard positions untenable for anything without a Monster or Vehicle keyword. Elite low-model-count armies can weather the volume by leaning on durable keyword-protected units, and anything that strips the transports before disembark denies both detachment payoffs entirely.
674: Built around Maulerfiends, Infractors in Chaos Rhinos, Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Defilers, winged Daemon Princes of Slaanesh, Flawless Blades, and Noise Marines, this is a transport-delivered melee beatdown that floods the midboard with threats across multiple threat vectors. The win condition is serial destruction — the Coterie of the Conceited detachment rewards making and meeting kill pledges each round with Pact points, so the list is engineered to continuously delete units through Maulerfiend charges and Rhino-disembarking Infractors crashing into whatever the fiends soften up. It punishes slower midboard armies that cannot efficiently remove multiple large targets simultaneously, overwhelming them through mobile anti-armour pressure and Flawless Blades Fights First timing. It cracks when fast alpha-strike lists strip the transports early or force failed pledges, collapsing the Pact point engine before it generates momentum.
672: Built around winged Daemon Princes of Slaanesh, Lord Exultants, Infractors, Tormentors, Defilers, Noise Marines in Chaos Rhinos, this is an aggressive mid-table brawler that floods the board with mobile threats across every phase. The engine is the Coterie Of The Conceited detachment's pledge mechanic — each round the Warlord bets a kill count, and meeting it banks Pact points, so the list is structured to reliably destroy enemy units in batches and keep the Pact economy running. Rhino-delivered Infractors and Noise Marines crack open infantry blobs while Defilers and Daemon Princes apply mobile anti-armour pressure simultaneously, punishing lists that spread damage across many unit types rather than concentrating it. The pledge mechanic punishes you hard when you can't deliver kills on schedule, meaning elite low-model-count armies that are difficult to remove can stall your Pact generation and leave you resource-starved mid-game.
675: Built around Infractors, Lords Exultant, Flawless Blades, Tormentors, Chaos Spawn, and Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, supported by Defilers and Noise Marines in Rhinos, this is a transport-heavy melee hammer that floods the midboard with threat vectors across multiple phases. The win condition is pile-driving Rhino-delivered infantry into contested objectives while Lords Exultant amplify Infractors into a kill chain that dismantles anything standing on priority ground. It punishes static gunlines and elite elite-footprint armies that can't generate enough overwatch or peel screens fast enough to stop multiple simultaneous assault waves arriving from different angles. Armies that can alpha-strike the Rhinos before disembarkation, screen all flanks against Spawn and Daemon Princes, and sustain enough firepower to attrition the melee units before they engage will crack this list open.
436: Built around Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Foetid Bloat-Drones (both variants), Poxwalkers as screening chaff, and a terminator core of Deathshroud and Blightlords supported by Lords of Contagion and Virulence, this list runs the Contagion Engines detachment to give all its daemon engines the ASSAULT keyword on ranged attacks — letting them shoot after advancing and press the midboard relentlessly. The win condition is attrition through layered lethality: daemon engines grind forward under Poxwalker cover, stacking Afflicted conditions that Death Lord's Chosen converts into passive mortal wound bleed every opponent Command phase while the terminators close for the kill. It punishes durable, slow armies that cannot clear the Poxwalker screens quickly enough to escape the Affliction engine before the mortal wounds compound. Faster, high-volume shooting lists that can strip screens early and prioritise the haulers before they reach optimal range will crack the pressure before it builds.
633: Built around Neophyte Hybrids, Achilles Ridgerunners, Patriarch, Purestrain Genestealers, Hyperadapted Raveners, Benefictus, Deathleaper, Acolyte Hybrids, and Atalan Jackals, this Final Day list fuses GSC's own horde core with borrowed Tyranid Vanguard muscle for a mid-board brawling mass that hits from every angle. The engine is layered threat saturation — Raveners and Purestrain Genestealers crash into melee while Ridgerunners and Hybrids hold ground and heal in terrain via Xenocult Masses, denying opponents clean target priority and forcing bad trades. It punishes elite low-model armies that can't answer simultaneous charges from multiple fast melee units and a regenerating screen. Armies with strong shooting chaff-clear and hard engagement denial can strand the close-combat wave before it lands, leaving the midfield screen to collapse under pressure.
688: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Interceptor Squads, Strike Squads, and Paladin Squads, this is a highly mobile psychic melee force that floods the mid-board with hard-hitting, teleport-capable units across multiple detachment flavors. The win condition is relentless positional pressure — Interceptors surge onto objectives while Dreadknights and Paladins crash into priority targets, with Paladin wound-bonus support and Leadership-gated Sustained Hits fueling a layered kill chain that punishes anything that lets Grey Knights touch it. It excels against slower, medium-toughness armies that can't deny board entry or absorb repeated elite melee threats across multiple vectors simultaneously. It cracks under concentrated anti-elite firepower and alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete Dreadknights before they engage, stripping the build of its primary damage engine.
634: Built around Atalan Jackals, Achilles Ridgerunners, Goliath Rockgrinders, and waves of Acolyte Hybrids with hand flamers, this is an Outlander Claw mechanised horde that floods the board with cheap, high-OC mounted bodies backed by layered shooting. The win condition is strangling objectives early: Jackals lock down controlled markers at end of Command phase before opponents can contest, while Ridgerunners and Rockgrinders pour anti-armour fire into anything threatening that grip, and Reductus Saboteurs disrupt enemy positioning ahead of the advance. It punishes static gunlines and elite low-model-count armies brutally — the sheer volume of Mounted and Vehicle models inflating OC makes displacement nearly impossible without dedicated melee. Aggressive melee alpha-strikes that reach the Jackals before they lock objectives, or high-volume anti-infantry fire clearing the hand-flamer Acolyte screens, can collapse the controlling pressure and leave the midboard exposed.
689: Built around multiple Purgation Squads, Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Castellan Crowe, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this list runs primarily the Fires of Purgation detachment with Brotherhood Strike as a common second pick. The win condition is forcing repeated battle-shock rolls — Purgation Squads pin enemy units via Righteous Persecution, triggering a battle-shock roll at -1, while deep-striking elements arrive with re-rolled hit and wound rolls of 1 under Brotherhood Strike to exploit anything that cracks. It punishes armies reliant on Leadership-sensitive abilities and coherent battleline control, since stacking pin-and-shock disrupts activation economy across multiple units simultaneously. Armies that can screen out Purgation Squad positioning or flood the board with high-Leadership, high-model-count units that absorb battle-shock results without consequence will blunt the engine's pressure.
690: Built around multiple Paladin Squads supported by Interceptor Squads, Strike Squads, a Brotherhood Chaplain, a Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight, and a Brother-Captain, this list runs the Banishers detachment with Argent Assault as its primary stacked enhancement — using the Chaplain to pass Leadership tests before fighting, granting Paladins either Sustained Hits 1 or improved wound rolls against high-Toughness targets when Argent Assault's +1 to wound kicks in. The win condition is aggressive mid-board control: Interceptors surge to contest and screen while the Paladin brick grinds through whatever they engage, with Psychic Celerity and Sixty-sixth Seal keeping key characters flexible and mobile. It punishes slow elite armies that can't avoid close combat, because the layered wound-roll buffs make the Paladins dangerous even into heavy armour and high-Toughness monsters. Horde lists and anything that can overload its melee with volume attacks or screen it off objectives crack this build open, since the relatively small model count struggles to contest multiple angles simultaneously.
474: Built around Grand Master Nemesis Dreadknights (nearly two per list), Castellan Crowe, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, Brotherhood Librarians, Paladin Squads, and Interceptor Squads, this is a mobile, multi-threat Grey Knights force with no single defining detachment. The win condition is layered pressure across multiple vectors — Dreadknights threaten heavy targets while Interceptors surge onto objectives and Purifiers punish clustered infantry, forcing opponents to react in multiple directions simultaneously rather than neutralising one key piece. It punishes lists that rely on static gunlines or tight unit coherency, overwhelming positional discipline with teleport-assisted repositioning and multi-angle lethality. It cracks when faced with armies that can isolate and delete the Dreadknights early, stripping the primary damage engine before the supporting cast can compensate.
582: Built around Inquisitor Kroyle, Subductor Squads, Imperial Navy Breachers, Navigators, Aquila Kill Teams, Callidus and Eversor Assassins, Deathwatch Kill Teams, Grey Knights Terminators, Sisters of Battle, Sanctifiers, and Rogue Trader Entourages, this is a dense combined-arms coalition spread across three detachment variants — Imperialis Fleet, Veiled Blade Elimination Force, and Ordo Hereticus Purgation Force. The list wins by layering lethal firepower from multiple elite infantry platforms simultaneously, using Imperialis Fleet's target-designation ability to focus kill priority and transport-delivered infantry to contest objectives under fire. It punishes mid-tier horde armies that can't absorb sustained gunline pressure from multiple angles across a mass of small elite units. However, it struggles against armies that can surgically isolate and delete its fragile individual squads before they mass their firepower, as the lack of a single durable anchor means coordinated alpha strikes can unravel the list piece by piece.
615: Built around Berehk Stornbröw, Einhyr Hearthguard, Cthonian Beserks, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn under the Hearthguard Covenant, this is a dense mid-board brawler that layers elite melee infantry with hard-hitting vehicle fire support. The core plan is to crash Beserks and Hearthguard into the enemy's face while Thunderkyn and Hekatons grind through armour, using the Covenant's wound re-roll aura within 9" to make every close-range engagement punishingly efficient. It punishes armies that rely on mid-tier toughness targets and slow defensive gunlines, where its combination of mobile skimmer harassment via Sagitaurs and Hernkyn Pioneers and relentless melee pressure overwhelms piecemeal. Armies that can reliably disengage, kite, or alpha-strike the Hearthguard before the 9" aura activates will strip the build's teeth before it can brawl.
700: Built around the Cerastus Knight Lancer, Knight Castellan, and Armiger Warglaives, Questoris Companions runs a mixed battlegroup of heavy and fast Knights under the Questoris Companions detachment, which rewards fulfilling Oaths by stacking additional ones each turn, compounding pressure across the game. The win condition is layered anti-armour aggression — Lancers crash into the enemy midfield while Castellans and Warglaives clear flanks, with cascading Oaths continuously generating bonuses that make each Knight progressively harder to ignore. This build punishes armour-heavy and elite lists badly, overloading threat saturation across multiple large-base models that each demand dedicated answers. It struggles against lists that can deny mobility or isolate and delete Knights one at a time before the Oath engine compounds, since losing key pieces early collapses the pressure cascade it depends on.
621: Built around Hekaton Land Fortresses, Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carriers, Sagitaurs, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn alongside a dense infantry core of Hearthkyn Warriors, Hernkyn Yaegirs, and Einhyr Hearthguard, this is a massed mid-board brawler that floods the table with bodies and armoured vehicles simultaneously. The plan is to push transports and skimmers into scoring positions early, use Arkanyst Evaluators and Memnyr Strategists to stack threat priority, then grind opponents off objectives through sheer volume of layered ranged fire backed by durable infantry that refuses to shift. It punishes armies relying on elite, low-model-count units, overwhelming them with attrition before they can generate enough output to clear the board. It cracks under hard alpha-strike pressure or armies that can surgically strip the transports early, stranding infantry in the open and collapsing the mid-board presence the entire scoring engine depends on.
617: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Kapricus Carriers, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, this is a mobile mid-board brawler that uses fast HERNKYN skimmer units to threaten every angle while heavy firepower grinds down what survives. The Farseekers detachment's +1 to hit rolls for HERNKYN ranged attacks within 12" rewards aggressive positioning, so the list earns its points by crowding the midfield, forcing enemies off objectives while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses punish anything that over-commits to clear them. It punishes slow, durable gunlines and elite infantry that can't shift volume threats quickly — layered lethality across multiple unit types means there's no single removal priority. Armies that can screen the 12" threat bubble or alpha-strike the Hernkyn skimmers before they close will strip the accuracy engine and leave the gunline elements fighting at degraded efficiency.
620: Built around Hernkyn Pioneers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Einhyr Hearthguard, this is a mid-board brawler that layers fast skimmer harassment with a durable armoured core. The Farseekers detachment's +1 to hit within 12" turns Hernkyn units into close-range precision instruments, so the plan is to surge Pioneer and Yaegir screens forward to contest objectives while Thunderkyn and Land Fortresses punish anything that pushes back. It thrives against armies that rely on staying at range or holding midfield passively — the combination of Kapricus Carriers ferrying Hearthkyn and a dense skimmer presence makes objective denial extremely difficult. Slower elite armies that can't clear the screen before the Hernkyn close the gap will be systematically dismantled, but high-volume, long-range shooting that strips the Pioneer screen before the Thunderkyn can engage leaves the gunline exposed and the +1 to hit bonus irrelevant.
619: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Hekaton Land Fortresses, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Ûthar the Destined operating under Hearthguard Covenant, this is a mid-table brawler that marches a wall of elite infantry and heavy armour into the opponent's face. The win condition is grinding through the scoring zones at close range — Hearthguard Covenant's wound-roll re-rolls inside 9" make the Hearthguard and Ûthar's close-range volleys brutally efficient, while Sagitaurs, Hernkyn Pioneers, and Kapricus Carriers provide the mobility and board coverage to contest objectives across the whole table. It punishes elite-infantry and vehicle-heavy lists that want to trade efficiently in the mid-board, because layered lethal firepower and durable multi-wound bodies make those trades deeply unfavourable. Horde armies that can swamp objectives before the Votann wall arrives, or fast alpha-strike lists that strip the transport screen early and isolate the Hearthguard out of their 9" threat bubble, can crack it open.
616: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Kâhl, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and a dense supporting cast of Beserks, Pioneers, Yaegirs, Hearthkyn Warriors, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and Sagitaurs, this Hearthband list floods the mid-table with tough, numerous bodies backed by layered fire support. The win condition is grinding forward into Engagement Range where Hearthband's AP improvement on Hearthguard and Kâhl attacks kicks in, using the horde's sheer volume to hold objectives while the Thunderkyn and vehicle gunline bleed opposing units from range. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't answer both the melee pressure and the sustained shooting simultaneously, turning AP efficiency into a war of attrition they can't win. It struggles against fast alpha-strike threats that can strip the mid-board screen before the AP bonuses ever matter, leaving the slower core units overextended and isolated.
618: Built around Sagitaurs (Scouts 6" courtesy of Armoured Trailblazers), Cthonian Beserks, Hernkyn Pioneers, a Hekaton Land Fortress, and a full suite of Votann infantry and support characters, this list floods the midboard with fast armour and hard-hitting foot soldiers from turn one. The Sagitaurs surge forward pre-game to contest midfield objectives early, while Beserks threaten counter-punch brawls and the Land Fortress anchors a punishing gun platform behind them. It punishes lists that rely on holding territory passively — the early Scout move denies safe objective setups and forces opponents to fight on awkward terms against layered firepower and melee threat. High-mobility alpha strike lists or anything with strong deep strike denial can disrupt the forward Scout push before the Beserks arrive to reinforce it.
623: Built around a Lieutenant with combi-weapon, Intercessors, and a Librarian cycling Psychic Disciplines through the Librarius Conclave detachment, this is a mobile Space Marines infantry force that layers psychic buffs onto a flexible, multi-unit battle line. The win condition is applying the right Discipline each round — Divination for re-rolling hits and wounds against priority targets, Pyromancy or Biomancy to shift threat angles — while infantry blocks contest mid-board objectives and combi-weapon firepower picks apart exposed units. It punishes passive gunlines and low-mobility armies by dictating engagement range, using cover-granting detachment rules and mobile screening to stay resilient while maintaining offensive output. It cracks open against elite melee armies or heavy alpha-strike lists that can collapse its relatively fragile infantry before the Disciplines engine compounds across rounds.
545: Built around Nekrosor Ammentar, Skorpekh Destroyers, Lokhust Destroyers, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, and a Skorpekh Lord, all supercharged by Cursed Legion's Destroyer Cult Strength bonus, with Lychguard, Plasmancer, and Overlord with Translocation Shroud providing support and the Void Dragon anchoring the heavy-hitting centre. The plan is to trigger the Cursed Legion cascade — kill or half-strength a unit to spike Strength again, then chain that bonus across multiple Destroyer units in the same turn, deleting threats that can't survive the escalating damage output while scoring through presence and board control. It punishes mid-density infantry and light-vehicle lists hard, where the Strength ramp turns already-efficient Destroyer weapons into overkill and the mobile toolkit keeps the threat spread too wide to contain. It cracks against elite armoured armies or deep-strike-heavy lists that can isolate and remove the Destroyer units before the kill-chain trigger fires, shutting down the snowball before it starts.
535: Built around Scout Squads screening forward, Sternguard Veterans hitting hard at range, Intercessors holding ground, and Librarians cycling Psychic Disciplines to buff the force each battle round, this is a Space Marines gunline that layers bodies, firepower, and adaptive psychic support across a spread detachment base. The win condition is controlling objectives early with scouts and cheap infantry while Sternguard and Ballistus Dreadnoughts — present in over 40% of lists — generate enough ranged kill pressure to deny enemy scoring. It punishes slower, heavier armies that can't clear durable, continuously-replenishing objective holders before the score gap opens. It cracks against fast aggressive armies that can collapse the screen before the gunline stabilizes, or elite melee threats that render the midboard infantry non-functional in close quarters.
455: Built around Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Doomsday Arks, Skorpekh Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, and the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, this Cursed Legion list is a mobile, multi-threat murder machine that chains high-Strength Destroyer Cult attacks into ever-escalating firepower — the detachment's kill-trigger rule pumps weapon Strength further each time a unit destroys or halves an enemy unit, rewarding aggressive sequencing. The plan is to use Doomsday Arks and Lokhust Heavies to crack hard targets at range while Skorpekh Destroyers and the Nightbringer crash into midfield, forcing opponents to answer threats from multiple angles simultaneously and bleeding secondaries in the process. It punishes lower-model-count elite armies that cannot absorb the Strength escalation chain and struggle to contest the wide threat vectors. It cracks open against high-volume screening lists that can deny the kill-trigger activations and starve the Destroyer cascade before it builds momentum.
659: Built around Transcendent C'tan, the Nightbringer, the Void Dragon, the Deceiver, Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list fields a murderer's row of demigod monsters backed by subsurface ambush infantry. The plan is to threaten every quadrant simultaneously — C'tan walk into midfield demanding answers while Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers emerge from underground to contest objectives and punish anything that peels away to deal with the gods. It brutalizes lists that can only answer one threat vector at a time, forcing impossible priority decisions against targets with elite durability and board-wide reach. It cracks when opponents bring redundant high-damage anti-monster shooting, because stripping through multiple C'tan before Reanimation can stabilize them will eventually outpace the list's threat density.
660: Built around Imotekh the Stormlord, the Silent King, and a wall of Monoliths backed by Lychguard, Triarch Praetorians, and Triarch Stalkers, this is an Obeisance Phalanx list that locks a target unit and funnels its entire Noble-Triarch-Lychguard kill chain into it with +1 to wound on every attack. The plan is to designate the most dangerous or valuable enemy unit each Command phase, then converge the full weight of that buffed melee and shooting corps to delete it while Monoliths hold and contest objectives. It punishes armies with elite, hard-to-crack anchor units — precisely the targets the wound-roll bonus dismantles fastest — and the mobile toolkit of Flayed Ones and Ophydian Destroyers keeps pressure on flanks simultaneously. Armies that can spread damage across the list and avoid presenting a single high-value target dilute the Obeisance trigger, and anything that can screen the backfield against the deep-striking harassment pieces reduces the board pressure this build relies on to force mistakes.
658: Built around the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, the Deceiver, and—in most lists—the Transcendent C'tan and Imotekh the Stormlord, this is a Pantheon of Woe monster-hammer list that floods the board with enormous, independently dangerous pieces. The win condition is straightforward brutality: Distortion Fields forces enemy units within 6" of any C'tan to suffer improved AP on every incoming attack, creating a damning dilemma where bunching to contest objectives accelerates their own destruction, while the C'tan themselves threaten nearly anything in melee or shooting. This build punishes elite, low-model-count armies badly—opponents relying on a handful of tough units get their armour bypassed by stacking AP improvement across multiple monster auras simultaneously. Its weakness is volume-of-attacks chaff lists that can bubble-wrap objectives and kite the slow monsters out of scoring positions, exploiting the build's limited board-coverage infantry presence.
569: Built around the Defiler as its lone consistent anchor, this World Eaters list fills out with a rotating cast of melee infantry, daemon engines, and support characters drawn from a wide pool of variable picks. The Defiler provides a mid-table threat that forces opponents to commit resources while infantry waves close in, scoring through kill pressure and board control rather than passive objective camping. It punishes gunline armies that lack reliable anti-tank overload, since the Defiler demands dedicated answers while screening infantry absorb attrition and contest secondaries. The build's inconsistency is its chief liability — with almost every supporting unit appearing in fewer than a third of lists, opponents who scout the pairing face a predictable core that's thin on redundancy if the Defiler dies early.
622: Built around Vertus Praetors, Allarus Custodians, and a Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike, this is a fast, elite melee force that floods the midboard with elite golden warriors backed by variable Knight and infantry support. The plan is to use jetbike speed and terminator deep strike threats to seize objectives early, then grind opponents off them through superior individual model durability and melee output. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot trade efficiently, as each Custodes unit demands a disproportionate investment of firepower to remove. It cracks open against high-volume mortal wound output or extreme ranged alpha strikes that can delete expensive individual units before their mobility and melee advantages can be realised.
603: Built around Gretchin screens, Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Flash Gitz, Tankbustas, and Ghazghkull Thraka, this is a horde gunline that floods the table with bodies while concentrating serious firepower from the back ranks. The win condition is using Gretchin and Boyz to screen objectives and deny approach lanes while Lootas, Flash Gitz, and Tankbustas punish anything that tries to push through, with Ghazghkull calling the Waaagh! to spike ranged output at the critical moment. It punishes slow, durable armies that want to walk up the table, because the sheer volume of shots combined with Tankbusta anti-tank overload strips vehicles and monsters before they can land. Aggressive alpha-strike lists that can crack the screening layers early and close distance before the Waaagh! fires are the real threat, since this army's shooting depends on having time to set up and the melee defence behind those screens is thin.
702: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, Flash Gitz, Boyz, Breaka Boyz, and Bannernobs operating under the Freebooter Krew detachment, this list blends a shooting-heavy midboard brawler with enough bodies to flood objectives. The engine is Freebooter Krew's loot objective designation combined with Sustained Hits 1 on every attacking unit, letting Flash Gitz and Boyz punish anything that contests the priority marker while Ghazghkull's Waaagh! amplifies the volume further; Battlewagons and Trukks push Breaka Boyz and Nobz into close-range fights to clean up survivors. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to screen a flooding horde while simultaneously outgunning them with Sustained fire. Armies that can delete key pieces at range before the horde closes — or that project enough durable bodies to drown the loot objective in contesting units — expose the list's middling resilience and mediocre damage ceiling.
677: Built around Vulkan He'stan, Adrax Agatone, and roughly two Infernus Squads per list, supported by Librarians, Bladeguard Veterans, and Land Raider Redeemers hauling elites into contact, this is a massed flame-and-fist brawler that punishes infantry-dense armies at close quarters. The win condition is delivering superheated payloads into tightly packed targets — He'stan and Agatone stack fire-weapon buffs onto Infernus Squads while Eradicators handle heavier targets and Bladeguard clean up whatever survives the burn. It punishes horde and gunline armies ruthlessly, overwhelming them with sheer volume of high-AP close-range shooting before they can reposition. Melee-heavy elite armies that can absorb the flame output and hit back before the Land Raider delivers its cargo will crack this list open.
678: Built around Marneus Calgar, Captain Titus, Bladeguard Veterans, Wardens of Ultramar, Victrix Honour Guard, Sternguard Veterans, and a Librarian cycling Psychic Disciplines round-to-round, this is a dense objective-holding gunline that layers elite infantry across the board. The win condition is controlling objectives early with durable, AP-buffed melee units under Reclamation Force — improving armour penetration in melee near objectives while tanking wounds back on markers you already own — then swapping Disciplines to Divination to spike Sternguard shooting when targets present themselves. It punishes horde armies and mid-tier armour through sheer volume of AP-improved attacks across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It cracks under concentrated alpha strikes that can isolate and delete its character-dependent blobs before the defensive layering comes online.
686: Built around Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, Land Speeders, Outriders, and Suboden Khan, this list uses the Fulguris Task Force's first-turn ingress move to flood the board with SPEEDER units before the opponent can react, backed by Scouts and Intercessors holding ground and a Lieutenant with combi-weapon providing command support. The win condition is early anti-armour pressure — Hammerstrikes and Land Speeders crack vehicles and heavy targets from turn one while mobile infantry lock down objectives. It punishes slow, tank-heavy gunlines that can't redeploy fast enough to answer threats arriving simultaneously from multiple angles. The vulnerability is dense screening or deep-strike denial, where opponents can block ingress lanes and force the Speeders into suboptimal positions, neutering the entire first-turn tempo swing that the build depends on.
681: Built around a psyker-heavy core of Librarians in Terminator Armour, Chief Librarian Tigurius, Bladeguard Veterans, Terminator Assault Squads, and Marneus Calgar, this list runs the Librarius Conclave detachment to cycle psychic disciplines each battle round — Divination for hit/wound rerolls when it needs reliability, Pyromancy or Biomancy when it needs mobility or raw output. The win condition is controlling objectives with durable Terminators and Bladeguard who gain improved AP on melee attacks through the Reclamation Force secondary detachment, then using the psychic discipline of the moment to amplify whichever unit needs to crack the current threat. It punishes mid-toughness elite infantry hard, where stacking AP improvement and Divination rerolls turns already strong melee into a guaranteed-kill engine. It cracks under pressure from mass high-AP shooting armies that can strip its expensive melee blocks before they reach objectives, since the defensive Reclamation Force protection only triggers on objectives already controlled — not on the approach.
685: Built around Librarians (including a Terminator-armoured variant), Sternguard Veterans, Outriders, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, and Suboden Khan operating under the Librarius Conclave, this is a highly mobile infantry-and-skimmer force that flexes its psychic discipline each battle round to suit the moment. The win condition is a relentless advance using Spearpoint Task Force's charge-after-Advance rule to crash Outriders and Terminator Assault Squads into priority targets, while Suboden Khan's post-fight 6" move lets him chain into a second threat after cleaning up a first. Scouts and Incursors screen forward objectives while Land Speeders and Hammerstrikes apply mobile anti-armour pressure across the table, punishing static gunlines that cannot reposition to answer threats from multiple vectors simultaneously. It cracks open when faced with durable, high-toughness targets that absorb the melee push and blunt the chain-kill engine before the psychic discipline bonuses can compensate for raw damage output.
679: Built around Victrix Honour Guard, Marneus Calgar in Armour of Antilochus, Cato Sicarius, Repulsor Executioners, and a screen of Intercessors, Scouts, and Incursors, this list locks into terrain features and fights from fortified positions under the Ceramite Sentinels detachment, gaining re-rolls to hit and wound on 1s plus the Entrenched keyword for any unit already settled inside cover. The win condition is a layered gunline anchored by multiple Repulsor Executioners delivering mobile anti-armour firepower while elite infantry bubble-wrap objectives and deny displacement. It punishes slower, medium-durability armies that cannot efficiently remove entrenched units turn after turn, letting the Repulsors freely delete armour and monsters while infantry hold ground. It cracks open against alpha-strike lists and high-mobility armies that can pressure multiple terrain pieces simultaneously, forcing units off cover before Entrenched can activate and stripping the re-roll engine mid-game.
695: Built around Logan Grimnar, multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, and Wolf Guard Headtakers, this is a Saga of the Great Wolf list that floods the mid-table with durable, elite infantry and a legendary dreadnought anchor. The plan is to use the rotating Hunting Pack buffs — particularly re-roll Advance and Charge rolls from Encircling Jaws — to pressure objectives with terminator-heavy bricks that are hard to shift and harder to ignore. It punishes elite-infantry and vehicle-light lists that can't generate enough AP or volume to chew through multiple terminator units simultaneously. It cracks under sustained high-volume anti-tank fire or mortal wound spam that bypasses armour saves across several activations, thinning the elite core before the charge engine can close.
684: Built around Librarians cycling Psychic Disciplines, Outrider Squads, Assault Intercessors (both foot and jump pack), Bladeguard Veterans, Hellblasters in Impulsors, and Suboden Khan, this list runs Librarius Conclave as its engine with Spearpoint Task Force in most lists to let advancing and falling-back units still declare charges. The win condition is flexible pressure across every phase — Divination Discipline supercharges Hellblasters and Outriders into reliable kill tools, while Suboden Khan's post-kill Normal move chains him into fresh engagements and the Spearpoint rule keeps the entire force perpetually threatening charges after repositioning. It punishes horde and mid-table infantry-dense armies by flooding the board with fast, high-volume melee threats that can advance and charge simultaneously, overwhelming screens before heavier pieces can respond. It cracks against elite anti-infantry gunlines that can delete the fast movers before they close, and against armies that can consistently lock or kite Suboden Khan to deny his post-fight movement chain.
680: Built around Caanok Var, Terminator Assault Squads, Sternguard Veterans, and Psyker support from both a Librarian and a Librarian in Terminator Armour, this list runs the Hammer of Avernii detachment backed by the Librarius Conclave, blending a heavy transport-infantry gunline with a close-range hammer threat. The win condition is Caanok Var's RECALCULATING ability — chain-designating new Oath of Moment targets as each dies, keeping the wound re-roll engine live across the whole game while Sternguard and Terminators grind through priority threats in sequence. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that present clear, singular target priority, since the Oath chain never goes cold and the Librarius Conclave's Divination Discipline stacks additional re-rolls onto already-favourable matchups. Armies that flood the board with cheap units dilute the Oath targeting economy, and anything that can strip Caanok Var early collapses the entire re-roll chain before it can snowball.
676: Built around Vulkan He'stan, Adrax Agatone, Infernus Squads, Eradicators, Bladeguard Veterans, and a Land Raider Redeemer operating under the Firestorm Assault Force detachment, this is a close-range fire supremacy list that turns every Adeptus Astartes ranged weapon into an Assault weapon with a Strength bonus inside 12". The win condition is closing aggressively — often using the Redeemer as a transport — to trigger that 12" Strength buff across massed flame and melta profiles, burning through infantry screens and heavy armour simultaneously while Librarians cycle Psychic Disciplines for situational bonuses like re-rolls or extra mobility. It punishes armies that rely on volume-of-fire infantry blobs, since the combination of high-Strength flamers and Eradicator melta at close quarters shreds both light and medium targets efficiently. Armies that threaten it at range before it closes, or that use deep strike denial and fast-moving hard targets to keep it beyond 12", will bleed its efficiency and expose how dependent the list is on that tight engagement window.
682: Built around Darnath Lysander, a dense core of Assault and standard Terminators, Bladeguard Veterans, Sternguard Veterans, Vanguard Veterans with jump packs, and multiple Librarians operating under the Emperor's Shield and Librarius Conclave detachments. The gameplan is to lock Oath of Moment onto a priority target and pour fully re-rolled wound rolls through Lysander's bubble into it while the Librarius Conclave rotates between Divination's additional hit and wound re-rolls, Biomancy's movement boost, or Pyromancy depending on the matchup phase. This build punishes armies with elite multi-wound infantry by stacking wound re-roll layers onto a single kill-chain, making individual targets evaporate while jump pack units and transports push secondary scoring. It cracks under pressure from alpha-strike or deep-strike denial lists that can strip Oath of Moment targets before the re-roll engine engages, and spread-out objective spam that exposes how slow the Terminator core genuinely is.
697: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Logan Grimnar, and Arjac Rockfist, this is a dense melee-and-armour hammer that layers elite infantry with Repulsor Executioner fire support. The plan is to crash Terminators and Headtakers into midfield under character support — Logan and Arjac amplifying their threat — while Bjorn and the Repulsor Executioners suppress armour and hold angles, generating kills that convert into scoring. It punishes slower, durable armies that can't clear massed elite bodies quickly, using weight of elite melee combined with mobile anti-armour to overload defensive resources. However, it struggles against fast aggression that picks apart its relatively slow advance before the hammer connects, and anything that strips its character bubble early collapses the kill chain.
528: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Blood Claws, Wolf Scouts, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, this is a mass-infantry horde running the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, cycling through its Hunting Packs each Command phase to buff the entire Adeptus Astartes battleline. The plan is to flood every quarter of the board with cheap bodies and durable multi-squad threats simultaneously, using Encircling Jaws to guarantee charges across multiple units while Grimnar and Bjorn anchor the midfield brawl and convert that presence into primary score. It punishes light-to-medium infantry armies that can't kill bodies fast enough, overwhelming screens and out-contesting objectives through sheer unit count before the opponent can cycle enough firepower. It cracks under elite anti-horde gunlines that can efficiently delete multiple units per turn, leaving the scoring engine too thin to trade effectively into the late game.
696: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and a dense supporting cast of infantry, this is a Saga of the Beastslayer force that floods the board with elite and horde bodies alike. The engine is straightforward: every Adeptus Astartes attack against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles gains Lethal Hits, so the plan is to park durable terminator bricks and named heroes into opposing centerpieces and grind them out through critical hit fishing while scouts and intercessors contest objectives. It punishes elite-heavy and character-reliant lists hard, where Lethal Hits continuously bypasses the wound rolls that keep expensive models alive. However, a spread-out mechanized or horde opponent can dilute the Lethal Hits payoff by simply keeping Characters and Vehicles at range, leaving this slow-moving infantry mass vulnerable to being outmaneuvered and bled off objectives.
698: Built around Librarians (with the Fusillade enhancement on the most popular copy), Sternguard Veterans, Logan Grimnar, Wolf Guard Terminators, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and Njal Stormcaller operating under the Librarius Conclave detachment, this is a psyker-amplified elite infantry force that floods transports with hard-hitting foot soldiers and leans on Psychic Disciplines — cycling between Divination's re-rolls, Biomancy's movement surge, and Pyromancy's ranged output — to flex its threat profile round to round. The Saga of the Great Wolf detachment layers on top in most lists, granting Hunting Pack buffs that enable aggressive Advance-and-Charge plays or sharpen shooting, letting the terminator and veteran blobs punch into midboard and clear objectives on contact. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't reposition, because the combination of transport mobility, discipline-switching, and high-quality re-rolled shooting means it floods the midfield faster than flat-footed armies can respond. Armies that can strip transports at range before the cargo disembarks — particularly mobile anti-tank lists — crack it open by stranding elite infantry in the open with no delivery mechanism.
614: Built around Commander Farsight, Coldstar Commanders, Crisis Sunforge and Starscythe Battlesuits, Enforcer Commanders, Fireknife Crisis suits, Riptides, Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinders, and Ghostkeels all running the Retaliation Cadre, this list weaponizes close-range shooting — every Battlesuit attack within 12" gains +1 Strength, and within 9" gains +1 AP on top of that. The win condition is crashing into your opponent's midfield early, forcing engagements inside 9" where the AP bonus kicks in and Crisis multi-meltas and flamers delete armour and infantry alike in the same activation. It absolutely punishes medium-armour lists that can't screen their tanks — those units get dragged into the kill zone and dismantled by overloaded anti-armour volume at AP that cracks them open. However, anything that can deep-strike denial, castle up at range, or alpha-strike the exposed Battlesuits before they close will crack this list, since it has almost no defense if its aggressive positioning is disrupted before the buffs come online.
