703: Built around Defilers, Forgefiends, Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, Tzaangors, and Sekhetar Robots, this list runs a dense, layered Thousand Sons force blending heavy vehicles with resilient infantry and psychic support across the Ritual Of Regeneration and Warpforged Cabal detachments. The plan is to grind forward behind a wall of bodies, manifesting Rituals to heal Psyker characters while Forgefiends and Defilers leverage Warpforged Cabal re-rolls — ideally within 6" of a Psyker — to crack armour and score through attrition. It punishes slow, low-mobility armies that cannot project pressure early, letting the gunline dictate range while Terminators and Rubrics hold mid-table. Aggressive alpha-strike lists that delete the Psyker bubble fast will collapse both the healing engine and the vehicle re-roll support simultaneously.
704: Built around Kairos Fateweaver, multiple Lords of Change, Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, and Screamers flooding the mid-board, this Changehost Of Deceit list blends elite daemon engines with a horde of Tzaangors into a layered, mobile threat package. The win condition is stacking mortal wound output through Psychic abilities across multiple units simultaneously while the 4+ invulnerable save aura from Daemonic Illusions keeps Psyker-adjacent models alive long enough to grind through objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to answer both the horde chaff screening the mid-table and the hard-hitting Scarab Occult Terminators crashing through their lines. Lists that can strip the Psyker bubble from outside 6" — particularly long-range precision or high-volume ranged spam — collapse the invulnerable save coverage and expose the underlying fragility of daemon infantry to mass fire.
599: Built around Biovores, Neurotyrant, Neurolictors, Lictors, Zoanthropes, Genestealers, and Norn Emissaries, this is a highly mobile, multi-vector swarm that floods every corner of the board simultaneously. The win condition is threat saturation — Lictors and Neurolictors materialize into scoring positions and force reactive trades while Genestealers and Norn Emissaries deliver lethal mid-table pressure, with Biovores providing backline chip damage to punish static screens. It punishes gunline armies that rely on fixed fire lanes, because the combination of infiltrating hunters and deep-striking bodies means there is no safe angle to castle and no turn where the opponent isn't responding to multiple simultaneous crises. However, elite melee armies that can absorb or outfight the individual strike packages in the mid-table crack it open, since the build's lethality depends on isolating targets rather than winning sustained slugging matches.
515: Built around biovores, maleceptors, tyrannofexes, exocrines, genestealers, hormagaunts, norn emissaries, hive tyrants, broodlords, lictors, and neurotyrants, this is Invasion Fleet Tyranids at its most toolbox-complete — a faction-wide Swiss Army knife blending heavy guns, synapse-buffed hordes, and elite melee strikers. The list wins by selecting its Hyper-adaptation at game start to match the opponent, then layering genestealers and hormagaunts as objective pressure while tyrannofexes and exocrines grind durable targets from range. It punishes mixed armies that can't efficiently address both elite melee threats and massed bodies simultaneously, with lictors and broodlords enabling sudden midboard strikes that force reactive, unfavorable trades. Where it struggles is against hyper-focused lists that exploit its spread-thin investment — deep alpha strikes or overwhelming single-phase damage can strip key synapse nodes before the Hyper-adaptation engine fully engages.
716: Built around Helbrutes, Exalted Eightbound, Khorne Berzerkers, Jakhals, Slaughterbound, Chaos Spawn, Khârn the Betrayer, Eightbound, and Maulerfiends operating under the Berzerker Warband detachment, this is a wall-to-wall melee swarm that floods every lane with bodies. The win condition is simple brutality: charge everything every turn, converting the Berzerker Warband bonus into +1 Attack and +2 Strength on every melee weapon across the entire army to grind opponents off objectives through sheer combat attrition. It punishes static, low-model-count elite lists that can't hold multiple engagement fronts simultaneously — Helbrutes and Maulerfiends provide mobile anti-armour to crack hard targets while infantry swarms contest everywhere else. It struggles against armies that can screen effectively and deny charges, or that project enough shooting to delete key units before they reach combat.
612: Built around Slaughterbound, Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, a Daemon Prince of Khorne, Jakhals, and Chaos Spawn, this list runs the Possessed Slaughterband detachment and plays pure melee aggression across every phase. The engine is Brazen Fury: when shooting kills a Possessed model, the unit surges up to D6" for free, turning incoming fire into advance tempo and funneling multiple melee threats into charge range simultaneously, while the Daemon Prince sharpens his attacks mid-fight with Cleave or improved AP via Vessels of Wrath. It punishes gunline armies brutally — the more shooting a opponent commits, the more surge moves they gift, accelerating exactly the contact the opponent is trying to prevent. It cracks open against fast objective denial lists that can screen key lanes and starve the surge mechanic, since if Possessed never take casualties, the free movement engine never fires.
495: Built around Khârn the Betrayer, Angron, Exalted Eightbound, Eightbound, Khorne Berzerkers, Jakhals, Slaughterbound, Chaos Spawn, and Masters of Executions running Berzerker Warband, this is a mass-assault horde that floods the table with cheap bodies and elite shock troops delivered in Chaos Rhinos. The win condition is the charge-turn power spike — Berzerker Warband's +1 Attack and +2 Strength on every charging unit turns even mid-tier chaff into a genuine threat, so the list tries to stack multiple charges per turn across multiple lanes to delete key targets and collapse the opponent's scoring. It punishes static gunlines and fragile elite armies that struggle to kill through volume, screening with Jakhals and Spawn while Angron and Exalted Eightbound smash priority targets. It cracks apart against armies that deny or punish the charge through strong overwatch, movement debuffs, or durable screens that stall the assault before the stat bonus can be cashed in.
